comment-hygiene.5d0634f6ac62d38e85797172b1dfb075d0f5f6ee:
schemaVersion: 1
name: comment-hygiene
description: Daily rolling check of code comments against the code they describe
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 45 6 * * *
template:
  title: Check the oldest code comments for staleness
  description: |
    Check a small batch of source files for stale or low-value comments and
    correct them with a comment-only diff. A batch whose comments are already
    accurate is a successful no-diff run with validated no-diff evidence.

    ## The standard

    Judge every comment against this standard. It is stated generically so it
    applies in any language:

    - Comments say why; the code says what. A comment that restates the code
      adds noise, not information.
    - Doc comments state the contract: what a caller may assume and must
      uphold, not how the implementation happens to work today.
    - A module or file header states the unit's responsibility in one or two
      lines, not its contents list.
    - A guard, workaround or surprising branch may cite the incident or
      constraint behind it; that is the comment most worth keeping accurate.
    - No history narration: no "previously", "now", "new", "changed to" or
      diary of edits. Version control already keeps that record, and narration
      goes stale first.
    - No commented-out code. Delete it; version control keeps it.
    - No TODO, FIXME or similar marker without an owner: a person, a task or a
      tracking reference that can actually be followed up.
    - Escape hatches state their reason: an unsafe block, a lint exception,
      a suppressed check, an `expect`-style assertion or the equivalent in the
      file's language says why it is safe or why the exception earned its place.
    - A stale comment is a bug: one that contradicts the code misleads every
      later reader and outweighs having no comment at all.
    - Keep density low. Never add a comment for its own sake, to show a file
      was visited, or to reach a quota; deleting a restating comment is a fix.

    Fix in this priority order: comments that contradict the code first, then
    history narration, then comments that restate the code, then the rest of
    the standard. Preserve the author's voice where a comment is kept.

    A repository may supply its own sharper standard through a
    `comment-hygiene` tag instruction (`[workflow.tag_instructions.comment-hygiene]`
    in its Orbit workflow configuration). When the run carries such an
    instruction, follow it where it sharpens or overrides the generic standard
    above, and name it in the execution summary. It never loosens the
    comment-only diff rule below.

    ## Select a batch (preparation, before admission)

    This task is minted as `proposed` without `context_files`, so it is not
    a backlog drain candidate and cannot hold the whole tree as an
    unknown-footprint task. Batch selection is pre-admission preparation:
    the task pilot (or an operator preparing the task by hand) follows the
    steps in this section, persists exactly the selected `file:` selectors
    as the task's `context_files`, and only then is the task approved to
    `backlog` for admission. That preparation write happens before any
    execution claim exists, so it is never the claimed write the claim
    safeguard refuses, and the effective footprint is established before
    any edit. Without a pilot or operator preparation the instance simply
    waits in `proposed`; it does not stall unrelated backlog work. The
    executing run does not re-select a wider batch: it checks the files
    its prepared `context_files` name (see "Use the prepared footprint").

    1. List tracked source files with `git ls-files`. Exclude generated,
       vendored, fixture and test-data files, generated trees and indexes,
       archives, and every additional exclusion the repository's own guidance
       names (its agent guide, contribution guide, linter or formatter
       configuration, or generated-file markers in the files themselves).
       Check each candidate against those exclusions before selecting it. Keep
       paths relative to the repository root. Do not assume any language,
       layout or file extension set beyond what this repository contains.
    2. Build the carried attempt state. List the newest completed instances with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["comment-hygiene"],"limit":60,"fields":["id"],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
       For each candidate, newest first, discover its artifacts before fetching
       any ledger: list the metadata-only artifacts projection with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","field":"artifacts","model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and fetch the ledger with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"comment-hygiene-ledger.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       only when that listing names `comment-hygiene-ledger.json`. Skip a task whose
       listing has no ledger without calling `orbit.task.artifact.get` for it,
       and ignore its prose summary; never order by execution-summary text. A
       `schema_version` 2 ledger carries `state`, a cumulative map from each
       path to its two most recent attempt rows, newest first. It already
       covers every older ledger, so stop at the first listed one you can read and
       start from its `state`. Layer the `files` rows of each
       `schema_version` 1 ledger fetched before it on top (all of them when no
       version 2 ledger exists). For each path keep only the two rows with the
       newest `attempted_on` (ties: the newer task). Drop paths that step 1 no
       longer lists. The history window is a read bound, not a retention rule:
       an attempt survives in `state` after its task leaves the window. If no
       ledger could be read at all — no completed instance, the artifact tools

dependency-freshness.8cfbbaa89a3f93bb4cf8af57ac8ec943004464e1:
schemaVersion: 1
name: dependency-freshness
description: Monthly inventory of outdated, unused and duplicate dependencies; files at most 3 proposed upgrade or removal tasks
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 0 9 1 * *
template:
  title: Check dependency freshness
  description: |-
    Inventory this workspace's direct dependencies and keep them moving in
    small steps. The durable outputs are the `dependency-freshness.json`
    artifact on this task and the proposed upgrade or removal tasks filed
    below; the execution summary is only an audit trail. This task files
    work; it does not upgrade, remove, or edit any dependency itself, and it
    never builds, tests, or times anything.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface, never direct lifecycle CLI
      subcommands (they skip agent provenance). Find the previous run with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["dependency-freshness","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and fetch its inventory with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"dependency-freshness.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Search coverage with
      `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<one distinctive token>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      (lexical search matches one substring: use a single distinctive token,
      never a multi-word phrase, and never treat a 0-hit multi-word query as
      proof that nothing covers a candidate). Inspect a candidate with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      List open dependency work with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["proposed","backlog","in-progress","review","blocked"],"tag":"dependency-freshness","limit":200,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    - File an upgrade or removal task (tool-created tasks start `proposed`)
      with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"context_files":["file:<manifest path>","file:<lockfile path>"],"complexity":"<assessed>","tags":["dependency-freshness"],"type":"chore","relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"priority":"<low|medium>","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Read each filed task back with `orbit.task.show` before recording it
      as delivered. Never file a candidate without `context_files` naming
      the ecosystem manifest and its lockfile. Tasks land in `proposed`.
      Do not approve them.
    - Static inventory only: no builds, tests, or timing runs in this task.
      Put throwaway scripts under `.orbit/tmp/` (`$ORBIT_SCRATCH_DIR`).
    - Never bump the repository's own package version, tag, or publish
      anything. Releases are the operator's.
    - Fail open. A run with no candidate above the bars below is a
      successful no-op when the inventory evidence is persisted.

    ## Detect ecosystems and inventory

    Detect every ecosystem this workspace actually uses from its tracked
    manifests and lockfiles; assume none. Labelled examples — use only the
    rows this repository matches and ignore the rest:

    - Rust example: manifests named `Cargo.toml` with `Cargo.lock`;
      outdated from the ecosystem's outdated report, unused declared
      dependencies from its unused-dependency report, and duplicate
      versions from the lockfile or its duplicate report.
    - JavaScript/TypeScript example: `package.json` with its lockfile
      (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, or `yarn.lock`); outdated,
      unused, and duplicate reports from the package manager or its
      audit tooling.
    - Python example: `pyproject.toml` (or setup files) with `uv.lock`
      or the lockfile the workspace uses; outdated, unused, and duplicate
      reports from the environment tooling.
    - Go example: modules declared in `go.mod` with `go.sum`; outdated
      from the module tooling's list of newer versions, and unused or
      duplicate entries from its tidy and verification reports.

    Use each ecosystem's own outdated, unused, and duplicate tooling where
    it is available. Record any tool that is unavailable as a gap in the
    artifact and the execution summary; do not guess its output. For each
    detected ecosystem, record in the artifact:

    1. Direct dependencies that are behind, split into major-behind and
       minor-behind, with the declared version, the locked version, and
       the newest version the tooling reports.
    2. Declared dependencies that no tracked source file imports or calls.
    3. Duplicate versions of one dependency in the lockfile.

    Count usage for prioritization: for each direct dependency, count its
    import or call sites in tracked source files (exclude vendored and
    generated trees and test-only code, and name the exclusions).

    ## Security exclusion

    Exclude anything already covered by a security advisory or an open
    advisory task; that work belongs to the security sweeps (the
    `security-review` default and the advisory sweep routine). Before
    filing, list open security work with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["proposed","backlog","in-progress","review","blocked"],"tag":"security-review","limit":200,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    and search each candidate's name with `orbit.search` (see above).
    A candidate whose only reason to move is an advisory is recorded in
    the artifact as excluded, with the advisory or task that covers it,
    and is never filed here.

    ## Read the changelog before filing

    Before filing an upgrade, read the upstream changelog or release
    notes between the current and target versions. Quote the breaking
    changes that apply to this workspace in the filed task's description,
    with the version range they came from. An upgrade whose notes cannot
    be read (no network or registry access for that source) is recorded
    in the artifact as deferred with that reason, not filed from memory.

    ## Prioritize and file

    Rank candidates by how far behind they are multiplied by how much
    they are used (the import or call-site count above): major-behind
    first, then minor-behind by usage. File at most 3 tasks per run:

    - One task per dependency, or one per tight family that must move
      together (name every member and why they move together).
    - Unused-dependency removals are grouped into one task listing every
      unused declared dependency to remove; that grouped task counts
      toward the 3-task cap.
    - Duplicate versions are filed only when the fix is a version bump
      of a direct dependency; a duplicate caused only by transitive
      versions is recorded in the artifact, not filed.

    Each filed task's description contains: the ecosystem, the manifest
    and lockfile paths, the current and target versions, the usage count,
    the quoted breaking changes that apply (upgrades only), and the
    duplicate or advisory checks that were run. Record the overflow in
    the artifact; the next run files it first after re-verifying.

    ## No network

    With no network or registry access, the run is a successful no-op
    that states why: still write the artifact with the ecosystems
    detected, the tooling gaps, and `network: unavailable` as the reason
    no target versions could be confirmed, and file no task.

    ## Handoff

    Write `.orbit/tmp/dependency-freshness.json` with `schema_version: 1`,
    the scan time, and per ecosystem: the manifest and lockfile paths,
    the tooling used or the gap recorded, every direct dependency with
    its declared, locked, and newest versions (or the no-network reason),
    the unused and duplicate lists, the excluded advisory-covered entries,
    the deferred entries with reasons, and each candidate's disposition
    (filed task ID, grouped-removal task ID, or overflow). Diff it
    against the previous run's artifact fetched above and record the
    delta (newly behind, newly current, removed) in the execution
    summary; absent or unreadable means this is the baseline run, say so.
    Attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/dependency-freshness.json","path":"dependency-freshness.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    The execution summary covers: the ecosystems detected, the tooling
    gaps, the counts behind (major and minor), unused, and duplicate,
    the advisory exclusions, every filed task ID, the overflow, and the
    delta against the previous run.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Ecosystems were detected from tracked manifests and lockfiles under `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`, `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`/`uv.lock`, and `go.mod` rows that apply, and `dependency-freshness.json` names the tooling used or records each unavailable tool as a gap.
  - The artifact `dependency-freshness.json` lists each direct dependency with declared, locked, and newest versions split into major-behind and minor-behind, plus the unused declared dependencies and duplicate lockfile versions, with an import or call-site count per dependency.
  - Dependencies covered by a security advisory or an open `security-review` task were excluded and recorded in `dependency-freshness.json`, and no task was filed for them in this run.
  - Each filed upgrade task quotes the breaking changes that apply from the upstream release notes between its current and target versions, and at most 3 tasks were filed, all `proposed` with a `spawned_from` relation and `context_files` naming the manifest and lockfile.
  - No repository package version was bumped, no tag was created, and nothing was published; the run edited no manifest or lockfile.
  - 'With no network or registry access the run wrote `dependency-freshness.json` with `network: unavailable` as the reason, filed 0 tasks, and finished with status `success`.'
  - The run attaches `dependency-freshness.json` to this task, diffs it against the previous run's artifact or states it is the baseline run, and the execution summary maps every candidate to a disposition.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - dependency-freshness
  - no-diff-expected
  required_tools:
  - orbit.search
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.artifact.get
  - orbit.task.artifact.put
  - orbit.task.list
  - orbit.task.show
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  status: backlog

doc-duties.29ad235d3f49b8009c7c578fb8d46f27d5828b44:
schemaVersion: 1
name: doc-duties
description: Daily rolling verification of workspace documentation against current behavior
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 30 6 * * *
template:
  title: Validate the oldest workspace documentation
  description: |
    Validate a small batch of documentation against the current repository.
    Correct factual drift and broken links or Markdown. A batch whose claims
    are already accurate is a successful no-diff run with validated no-diff
    evidence.

    ## Select a batch

    1. List tracked Markdown files under `docs/` and tracked top-level
       `README*` or `CONTRIBUTING*` documents with `git ls-files`. Exclude vendored
       dependencies, generated trees and indexes, archives, and files the
       repository identifies as generated or historical records. Use repository
       guidance for any additional documentation scope; do not edit unrelated
       files. Keep the paths relative to the repository root.
    2. Build the carried attempt state. List the newest completed instances with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["doc-duties"],"limit":60,"fields":["id"],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and read each one's ledger, newest first, with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"doc-duties-ledger.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
       Skip a task with no ledger (a run from before ledgers existed) and ignore
       its prose summary; never order by execution-summary text. A
       `schema_version` 2 ledger carries `state`, a cumulative map from each
       path to its two most recent attempt rows, newest first. It already
       covers every older ledger, so stop at the first one you can read and
       start from its `state`. Layer the `documents` rows of each
       `schema_version` 1 ledger read before it on top (all of them when no
       version 2 ledger exists). For each path keep only the two rows with the
       newest `attempted_on` (ties: the newer task). Drop paths that step 1 no
       longer lists. The history window is a read bound, not a retention rule:
       an attempt survives in `state` after its task leaves the window.
    3. Give each candidate an ordering date, oldest first. Precedence: the
       latest carried `attempted_on` for that path (source `ledger`); else a
       valid `last_validated: YYYY-MM-DD` in existing YAML frontmatter (source
       `frontmatter`); else the date part of `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <path>`
       (source `git`). A candidate falls back to frontmatter or git only when
       no carried row names it. Report invalid frontmatter values and missing git
       history rather than treating them as real dates. If no ledger could be
       read at all (no completed instance, or the artifact tools failed), say so
       explicitly in the execution summary and the ledger `notes`; do not fall
       back silently.
    4. Escalate repeat skips. A candidate whose two most recent carried rows
       both have outcome `skipped` or `partial` is not selected. List it in the
       execution summary as needing its own task (for example section-by-section
       validation of an oversized document) with both reasons. Optionally file
       that task: first search `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<the path>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and skip the path when an open task already names it, then
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"Validate <path> section by section","description":"<why it was skipped, with the ledger reasons>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","type":"chore","tags":["docs","doc-duties-escalation"],"context_files":["file:<path>"],"relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"priority":"low","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
       A later `clean` or `fixed` row for the path ends the escalation.
    5. Sort the remaining candidates by ordering date, oldest first, breaking
       ties by relative path. Take at most six. If no candidates have a usable
       date, explain why in the execution summary and finish without a diff.

    ## Validate and record

    For each selected document, check factual claims against current source,
    commands, configuration, and related documentation. Correct verified drift,
    genuine spelling errors, and broken Markdown or relative links. Preserve
    the author's style and avoid unrelated rewrites. If a claim cannot be
    checked, leave it unchanged and record the limit. Give every selected
    document exactly one outcome:

    - `clean`: fully verified, no change needed.
    - `fixed`: fully verified, and drift was corrected.
    - `partial`: some claims verified, others left unchecked.
    - `skipped`: not verified (for example too large for this run), with a reason.

    Update `last_validated` to today's date only when that key already exists
    and the outcome is `clean` or `fixed`. Never add YAML frontmatter or a
    `last_validated` key to a document that lacks it, and leave it alone on
    `partial` and `skipped`.

    ## Attach the ledger

    Write `.orbit/tmp/doc-duties-ledger.json` and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/doc-duties-ledger.json","path":"doc-duties-ledger.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Its shape is `{"schema_version":2,"run_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","head":"<full HEAD commit SHA>","notes":"<optional, for example that no prior ledger was readable>","documents":[{"path":"<repo-relative path>","attempted_on":"YYYY-MM-DD","outcome":"clean|fixed|partial|skipped","reason":"<required unless clean or fixed>","ordering_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","ordering_source":"ledger|frontmatter|git"}],"state":{"<repo-relative path>":[{"attempted_on":"YYYY-MM-DD","outcome":"clean|fixed|partial|skipped","reason":"<as above>"}]}}`.
    Include one `documents` row per selected document, in selection order, and
    attach the ledger even when every document was skipped. `attempted_on` is
    today's date for every selected document regardless of outcome: it is what
    moves a skipped document to the back of the queue. Documents held back by
    the repeat-skip rule are not selected and get no `documents` row.
    `state` is the step 2 carried state after this run: for each selected
    document, put its new row first and keep only the two newest rows for that
    path; carry every other path's rows unchanged. Write it in full every run,

       guidance for any additional documentation scope; do not edit unrelated

       `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["doc-duties"],"limit":60,"fields":["id"],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and read each one's ledger, newest first, with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"doc-duties-ledger.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.

       its prose summary; never order by execution-summary text. A
       `schema_version` 2 ledger carries `state`, a cumulative map from each
       path to its two most recent attempt rows, newest first. It already
       covers every older ledger, so stop at the first one you can read and
       start from its `state`. Layer the `documents` rows of each
       `schema_version` 1 ledger read before it on top (all of them when no
       version 2 ledger exists). For each path keep only the two rows with the

escape-to-guard.dd80c010afa6ca947ff080c0f3da28522dedd1b9:
schemaVersion: 1
name: escape-to-guard
description: Weekly classification and clustering of recent regressions, filing at most 3 proposed mechanical guard tasks for classes of 3 or more regressions in 30 days that share one mechanism
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 40 7 * * 1
template:
  title: Turn recurring regression classes into mechanical guards
  description: |-
    Classify this workspace's recent regressions, cluster them by
    nature, escape and layer plus one shared mechanism, and file at most
    3 proposed guard tasks for clusters of 3 or more regressions in
    30 days. The durable outputs are the classifications recorded on the
    regression links, the filed guard tasks, and the
    `escape-to-guard.json` artifact; the execution summary is the audit
    trail. A workspace with no regression links is a successful no-op.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Use only Orbit's own analytics, task and search tools, plus git.
      Never read or edit Orbit state files, the Orbit database, or task
      files by hand, and never change a task's status. Read regression
      evidence with
      `orbit tool run orbit.codebase.analytics --input '{"window":"7d","min_support":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
      again with `"window":"30d"`, and once per escape value that needs
      isolation with `"escape":"unclassified"` and `"escape":"absent"`
      in the 30d call. Analytics ranks culprit tasks by their completion
      window and caps path drill-downs; it is context, not a complete
      census of regression tasks filed in the window. Inspect a task with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Search with
      `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<one distinctive token>","kind":"all","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      (task search matches the query's terms in any order, and friction
      search matches one case-insensitive substring: pass a single
      distinctive token, never a multi-word phrase, and never treat a
      0-hit multi-word query as proof that nothing covers a cluster).
      Find the previous run with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["escape-to-guard","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      (tag filters use AND semantics) and read its artifact with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"escape-to-guard.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    - Before filing a task, read the installed `orbit` skill's
      task-authoring reference (`references/task-authoring.md`) and
      follow it for task shape. Tool-created tasks start `proposed`;
      leave them `proposed` and never approve one.
    - Fail open. A window with no regression links, or with no cluster
      at the bar below, is a successful no-op. Do not invent work to
      justify the run.

    ## Classify unclassified and absent escapes

    Pin the scan timestamp before reading evidence. Build a complete link
    ledger with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --full --input '{"fields":["id","created_at","relations","context_files","status"],"limit":200,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Keep `--full`: the CLI's default compact output removes relations and
    context files even when the tool input requests them. Direct MCP callers
    request the same fields without this CLI flag. Verify every returned
    record has an ID, creation timestamp, status, and array-valued `relations`
    and `context_files`; a missing field is a read failure, never zero links.
    When `truncated` is true, repeat this same read with `limit` at least the
    returned `total`, increasing it again if new tasks arrived. The default list view
    has no pagination cursor or offset. Proceed only when `truncated` is false
    and the number of records equals `total`. If a complete read is unavailable,
    record the evidence gap and stop without claiming a no-regression no-op or
    filing guards. Do not treat truncated rankings or lists as complete.
    Keep each `regression_from` link whose
    regression task's `created_at` lies in the pinned 30d window, including
    links to culprits that landed earlier. Deduplicate by regression task
    ID plus culprit task ID. The 7d set is the subset filed in the pinned
    last 7 days. Use the analytics payloads for context and cross-checks;
    record their different population separately from this ledger.

    Count ledger links by escape before any classification, showing
    `unclassified` and `absent` separately. For every unclassified or
    absent link in the 7d set:

    1. Read the regression (fix) task and the culprit task it links to
       with `orbit.task.show`. The regression task's description, its
       landed paths, and its tags name what broke and where the fix
       sits.
    2. Read the culprit's landed diff. Resolve its landing commit with
       `git log --all --oneline --grep=<culprit task ID>` and read the
       diff with `git show <commit>`. When no commit names the culprit,
       read the delivery record through
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<culprit task ID>","field":"delivery","model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and show the landed SHA it names. Labelled example only: a diff
       that changes a serialized field's default with no migration of
       stored values points at a `contract_drift` nature and a
       `no_test` escape when no test covers stored-value reads.
    3. Pick one nature and one escape from the lists below, from that
       evidence alone. Choose `unclassified` rather than guess.

    `nature` is what kind of regression the link records:
    - `broke_existing`: the culprit broke behavior that worked before it landed.
    - `defect_in_new`: the defect is in code the culprit itself introduced.
    - `incomplete`: the culprit shipped without part of what its task required.
    - `merge_reintroduced`: a merge restored code or assets an earlier change had removed.
    - `contract_drift`: docs, schemas or a contract drifted from the behavior the culprit shipped.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the nature.
    `escape` is why the delivery gates missed it:
    - `no_test`: no test covered the broken behavior.
    - `test_not_selected`: a covering test existed but the delivery's gates did not run it.
    - `platform_only`: it shows only on a platform or host the gates did not exercise.
    - `review_missed`: it was visible in the diff and review did not flag it.
    - `spec_ambiguous`: the task or spec left the expected behavior open to the shipped reading.
    - `nondeterministic`: it depends on timing, ordering or environment and passed when gated.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the escape.

    Record each settled classification through the supported relation
    write: read the regression task's current `relations`, then send
    the full replacement list, preserving every existing relation and
    adding `"regression":{"nature":"<nature>","escape":"<escape>"}` to
    its `regression_from` entry, with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.update --input '{"id":"<regression task ID>","relations":[{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>","regression":{"nature":"<nature>","escape":"<escape>"}}],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    (the payload shows the one classified entry; send every existing
    relation, not only that entry). Read the task back and confirm the
    classification took effect. If that write refuses, or the read-back
    shows the stored classification did not change, record that link as
    unsettled in `escape-to-guard.json` with the refusal or the read-back
    value, proposed nature and escape, and supporting evidence. Never retry
    a terminal-task refusal or change lifecycle state to permit a write.
    A refusal alone does not prove a missing capability: inspect the
    supported tool schema and refusal reason. When those establish that no
    supported write can change an existing link (including an immutable
    terminal task), retain its classification in the artifact and file
    that capability gap once. Transient or link-specific failures stay
    unsettled in the artifact, without a speculative gap task. Search first
    with one distinctive token from
    the gap (for example `re-classify`) and inspect every plausible
    hit in every status; when no task already tracks it, file one
    with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"Support re-classifying an existing regression_from link","description":"<markdown naming the refused write, the read-back evidence, and the classifications held in escape-to-guard.json>","acceptance_criteria":["1 task update call changes the nature and escape stored on 1 named existing regression_from link and a task read-back shows the new values"],"context_files":["file:<verified path the write surface lives in>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["escape-to-guard","no-auto-approve"],"type":"chore","relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    File that gap at most once across all runs: a later run that finds
    it already tracked records the tracking task ID in the artifact
    and files nothing. The gap task does not count toward the guard
    cap below.

    After the classification loop, re-run `orbit.codebase.analytics` with
    `{"window":"30d","min_support":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}`, then again
    with `"escape":"unclassified"` and `"escape":"absent"`, to take the
    analytics after counts for the artifact. Re-read the same ledger tasks'
    relations to count stored classifications after the writes, keeping the
    pinned population fixed. Record artifact-held classifications separately
    from stored counts; never present an unpersisted choice as a stored
    change. Cluster the refreshed ledger, using an evidence-backed
    artifact-held classification where no supported write exists and
    labelling its source, so every settled link counts under its new
    nature and escape.

    ## Cluster by nature, escape, layer and mechanism

    Group every regression link in the pinned 30d ledger, classified or not,
    by nature x escape x layer. The layer is the fix layer the
    analytics payload reports for the regression task (its landed
    paths, else its declared footprint, else `unknown`). To recover a
    dimension missing from the capped analytics rows, use
    `orbit tool run orbit.codebase.show --input '{"path":"<verified culprit footprint path>","window":"all","min_support":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    and match the culprit and regression IDs. If no row reports the layer,
    state a consistent repository module layer from the verified fix paths
    and label that inference; use `unknown` when no fix paths exist. Inside each
    group, split by mechanism: read enough of each regression task and
    culprit diff to state the shared mechanism in one line, for
    example (labelled examples only) a serialized default changed
    without a migration, path normalization that differs on one host
    operating system, or a command-output golden that was not
    regenerated. A group whose members share no one-line mechanism is
    several clusters, not one. Record every cluster in the artifact
    with its nature, escape, layer, mechanism line, 7d and 30d counts,
    and every regression task ID in it.

    ## File guards for clusters at the bar

    A cluster gets one proposed guard task when it holds 3 or more
    distinct regression tasks in 30 days sharing the one mechanism (several
    culprit links from one regression count once toward the bar). File at most
    3 guard tasks per run. Rank qualifying clusters by 30d count, then
    by 7d count, and record clusters past the cap in the artifact as
    overflow for the next run.

    The guard is one mechanical check inside the gates that already
    exist, chosen from:
    - a lint rule or lint configuration entry the existing lint gate runs;
    - a type, newtype or other compile-time shape the existing build rejects when violated;
    - a static guard script invoked by an existing gate command;
    - a generator check that fails when generated output is stale;
    - a skill or review-instruction line, only for a `review_missed` cluster;
    - a regression test at the public boundary the broken behavior crosses, only for a `no_test` cluster (that task is a bug fix).

    Never propose a new required GitHub status check, a new merge
    gate, a new CI job that a merge waits on, or a human-only review
    step. Orbit ships with no merge gates on purpose: the guard must
    use a command the workspace already runs before landing; a skill or
    review-instruction line belongs to the existing review procedure.

    Before filing, search for duplicates: list open work with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["proposed","backlog","in-progress","review","blocked"],"tag":"escape-to-guard","limit":200,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
    then search one distinctive token from the mechanism per candidate
    cluster and inspect every plausible hit. A cluster already covered
    by an open or proposed task gets no new task; record the covering
    task ID in the artifact. Check rejected guard tasks the same way
    and refile only when the evidence has materially changed, saying
    what changed in the new task's description.

    File each guard (tool-created tasks start `proposed`) with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"Guard: <mechanism in one line>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"context_files":["file:<verified path>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["escape-to-guard","no-auto-approve"],"type":"feature","relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Set `type` to `bug` for a `no_test` regression-test guard and to
    `chore` for a `review_missed` skill or review-instruction guard;
    keep `feature` for the other guard kinds. The `no-auto-approve`
    tag keeps the task `proposed` for human approval. The description
    names:
    - at least 3 regression task IDs from the cluster as evidence, with each regression's culprit task ID;
    - the one-line mechanism and the cluster's nature, escape and layer;
    - the guard: the exact check, the existing gate command that runs it, and the violation it now rejects;

    ## Follow up earlier guards

    List guard tasks filed by earlier runs with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"tag":"escape-to-guard","limit":200,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    and keep only guard tasks (the `Guard:` title and mechanism identify
    them), excluding earlier `no-diff-expected` chores and the capability-gap
    task. For each landed
    guard, read its actual landed commit and timestamp through
    `orbit.task.show` with `field: "delivery"`, checking the landed commit
    with git. A `done` history timestamp alone is not landing evidence;
    report unavailable landing evidence as unknown. Then count regressions in its cluster
    (same nature, escape, layer and mechanism) whose regression task
    was created after that date, from the pinned 30d ledger and
    the regression tasks themselves. Record per guard: guard task ID,
    landed date, cluster, recurrence count after landing, and the
    recurring regression task IDs, and the observation window (only the
    available 30d window, not a claim about all time). A guard with 1 or more recurrences
    is evidence its check does not cover the mechanism: say so in the
    summary and let the cluster compete for this run's guard cap as a
    strengthened guard, naming the landed guard task in the new task's
    description.

    ## Record the run

    Write `.orbit/tmp/escape-to-guard.json` (`$ORBIT_SCRATCH_DIR`) with:
    - `schema_version: 1`, the scan timestamp, and the 7d and 30d window bounds;
    - `classification_counts`: stored ledger links counted before classification and after it, per escape value, with `unclassified` and `absent` shown separately, plus separately labelled analytics counts;
    - `classifications`: per-link before and after values, proposed nature and escape, evidence, persistence source, and any unsettled write refusal or read-back value;
    - `clusters`: every cluster row (nature, escape, layer, one-line mechanism, 7d count, 30d count, regression task IDs, disposition: filed task ID, covering task ID, overflow, or below the 3-in-30-days bar);

    - `previous_run_diff`: previous task ID or baseline reason, new and persistent clusters, those dropping below the bar, and the unclassified-plus-absent count change.

    too; a first page is not proof that no guard exists.

    (found through the previous-instance query above; absent or
    unreadable means this is the baseline run, so say so): name
    clusters that are new, clusters that persisted, clusters that
    dropped below the bar, and how the `unclassified` plus `absent`
    count moved. Attach the file with

    after classification counts, every cluster with its disposition,

schemaVersion: 1
name: friction-curation
description: Daily evidence-first deduplication, verification, resolution, and task filing for open friction records
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 15 7 * * *
template:
  title: Curate open friction records
  description: |-
    Curate the complete open-friction corpus in this workspace. The durable output is friction status changes and fix tasks; the execution summary is only an audit trail.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Never hand-edit friction records on disk. Agents must use the registered Orbit tool surface so status and body changes go through the store: `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","body":"<replacement markdown>"}'` to edit a body, and `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","status":"resolved"}'` to resolve one. `orbit.friction.resolve` is an operator-only CLI/dashboard tool (`orbit friction resolve <id>`) that this routine cannot call; the `update` form above stamps the same resolution metadata.
    - Frictions are a first-class `orbit search --kind friction` corpus (lexical only; hybrid remains task/doc). Snapshot the full open set with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.list --input '{"status":"open","limit":500,"offset":0,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`; keep paging until a page is shorter than the limit. Use `orbit search '<term>' --kind friction --all --json`, or `q` in the `orbit.friction.list` JSON input with `status: "open"`, to retrieve likely matches when grouping candidates. `--q` / lexical search match one case-insensitive substring: pass a single distinctive token (`EnvGuard`), never a multi-word phrase. A 0-hit whitespace-containing query is a substring miss, not proof the group is empty — retry each token on its own and read any `notes` on the empty result.
    - Search task coverage with `orbit search '<one distinctive symptom or component token>' --kind task --all --json`, then inspect plausible matches with `orbit task show <id> --json`. Do not treat a 0-hit multi-word task search as "no existing task"; retry single distinctive terms and read `notes` before certifying coverage.
    - Treat rejected tasks as historical coverage for deduplication and audit mapping, even though they are not active coverage. For every plausible rejected task, inspect the latest rejection rationale from `orbit task show <id> --json` (including its newest history/comment evidence) before deciding the friction's disposition; do not infer meaning from the status alone.
    - Before filing any fix task, read the installed `orbit` skill's task-authoring reference (`references/task-authoring.md`) completely. Follow it as the authority for general task shape, quality, provenance, and lifecycle rules. Do not duplicate that workflow here. Keep these friction-specific requirements: use the current workspace path; include evidence/reproduction and canonical modification-target `context_files`; add the `friction-curation` tag; and add exactly one `{"type":"resolves","target":"<canonical-friction-id>"}` relation for the canonical friction.
    - After every task creation, immediately read it back with `orbit.task.show <task-id> --json` (or the equivalent `orbit.task.show` tool) and verify that its relations contain exactly one `{"type":"resolves","target":"<canonical-friction-id>"}` edge. A task with a missing or incorrect edge does not count as coverage: repair its relations through `orbit.task.update` before continuing, then read it back again and verify the repaired edge. Filing a task does not itself fix the friction: leave that friction open. The relation resolves it only when the task reaches `done`.
    - Classify every rejected covering task after inspecting its latest rationale. A **terminal rejection** (intentional behavior, accepted ADR or policy decision, duplicate, obsolete report, or explicit won't-fix) can support closure only after appending a CLI/store resolution note that names the rejected task and cites the decision evidence, then resolving the friction through `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","status":"resolved"}'`. An **administrative rejection** (wrong workspace, malformed or mixed scope, stale evidence, or re-homing/re-authoring required) does not fix the friction: keep it open, record the `<friction-id> -> <rejected-task-id>` mapping and the required next action, and never describe it as fixed. When the current workspace owns the issue, file at most one correctly scoped active replacement; otherwise report the re-home need without creating a wrong-lane task.
    - If a proposed fix task widens a fail-closed guard, its description and acceptance criteria must enumerate the neighboring rejection guarantees that must remain rejected (wrong workspace, malformed or mixed scope, stale evidence, re-homing/re-authoring required, and any other adjacent invalid case found during inspection) and require validation evidence for each preserved rejection. A positive reproduction alone is insufficient.
    - Fail open. Zero open frictions or a fully current corpus is a successful no-op. When evidence is genuinely ambiguous, leave the friction open and report what remains unknown.

    ## Pass

    1. Snapshot every open friction using the paginated list command above.
    2. Dedupe by underlying issue, not wording, across active, done, and rejected task history. For each group, retain the earliest well-evidenced record as canonical unless a later record materially improves the reproduction. Preserve each duplicate's existing body, append a short resolution note naming the canonical friction id and the matching evidence, then use `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","body":"<resolution note>"}'` followed by `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","status":"resolved"}'`. Re-query the group with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.list --input '{"status":"open","q":"<one distinctive term>","model":"<agent-family>"}'` to confirm only the canonical record remains open. Never treat a 0-hit multi-word `--q` as a clean group.
    3. Verify every surviving open friction against the current tree and current executable behavior. Cite exact files/lines, command output, tests, run ids, or version state. If it no longer reproduces, preserve the body, append the checked evidence and resolution reason, and resolve it with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","status":"resolved"}'`. If it is still real, retain it open with the evidence gathered for task filing. Do not guess.
    4. For every verified-real survivor, search existing tasks using the task search/show commands above, including rejected tasks as historical coverage, and inspect the latest rejection rationale for every plausible rejected match. If active or done coverage clearly covers it, do not file a duplicate; record the auditable `<friction-id> -> <task-id>` mapping in the execution summary. If a rejected task has a terminal disposition, append the required resolution note naming that task and decision evidence, then resolve with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","status":"resolved"}'`. If its rejection is administrative, keep the friction open, record the rejected-task mapping and next action, and never claim it is fixed; file at most one correctly scoped active replacement only when this workspace owns the issue. If no task covers the survivor, follow the `orbit-task` skill's Create workflow and create exactly one fix task with reproduction evidence and the friction-specific workspace, canonical `context_files`, `friction-curation` tag, and `resolves:<canonical-friction-id>` relation requirements above. Complete the mandatory read-back and repair loop before recording the new `<friction-id> -> <task-id>` mapping. Never resolve a friction merely because its fix task was filed; it remains open until the resolving task reaches `done`.
    5. Repeat the same friction queries and coverage checks before finishing. The repeat pass must produce no further status changes and no duplicate tasks. Record counts and an auditable task-to-friction mapping for every canonical, resolved, verified, covered, created, and still-ambiguous id in this task's persisted `execution_summary`.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Every open friction was deduplicated against active, done, and rejected task history and evidence-checked against the current tree or behavior; every plausible rejected task's latest rejection rationale was inspected before disposition, and ambiguous records remained open.
  - Every resolved duplicate names its canonical friction id, and every no-longer-reproducing resolution records the evidence and reason through the CLI/store surface.
  - Every terminally rejected covering task has a CLI/store resolution note naming the rejected task and decision evidence before its friction is resolved; administrative rejections leave the friction open, record the rejected-task mapping and next action, and create at most one correctly scoped active replacement.
  - Every verified-real friction is covered by exactly one active or done Orbit task, or by a terminally rejected task with the required resolution evidence; new tasks carry reproduction evidence and exactly one verified `resolves` relation to the canonical friction without prematurely resolving the friction.
  - Every newly filed task is read back and repaired through `orbit.task.update` if its exact `resolves` relation is missing or incorrect before it counts as coverage.
  - Every task proposing to widen a fail-closed guard enumerates the neighboring rejection guarantees that must remain rejected and includes validation evidence for each preserved case.
  - A repeat pass makes no status changes and files no duplicate tasks, and its persisted execution summary contains an auditable task-to-friction mapping; an empty or already-curated corpus succeeds as a no-op.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - friction-curation
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  # The portable system lane is seeded per machine and compatibility-aliased
  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog

name: full-code-review
description: Whole-codebase white-box review at one pinned integration-branch commit, fanned out as one review chore per area
enabled: false
schedule:

template:
  title: Coordinate a full codebase review
  description: |-
    Coordinate a whole-codebase white-box review of this workspace at one pinned
    commit of its integration branch. You do not review code yourself: you pin
    the commit, partition the tree into review areas, and file one area-review
    task per area. The durable output is those filed tasks; the execution summary
    is the audit trail. Narrative-only output does not count as delivery.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface. List area reviews already in flight with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["backlog","in-progress","proposed","blocked","review"],"type":"chore","tag":["full-code-review","no-diff-expected"],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      File an area review with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"<medium|hard>","type":"chore","tags":["full-code-review","no-diff-expected"],"context_files":["dir:<area directory>"],"required_tools":["orbit.search","orbit.task.add","orbit.task.show","orbit.task.artifact.get","orbit.task.artifact.put"],"relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"priority":"medium","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Area tasks carry exactly the tags `full-code-review` and `no-diff-expected`.
      Never tag one `code-review`: completed `code-review` chores are the
      incremental review sweep's cursor records, and an area review there would
      be mistaken for a sweep.
    - Area tasks have complexity `hard` at most, never `xhard`, and no `crew`,
      so each is routed by automatic selection.
    - This coordinator and its area reviews are `no-diff-expected`, in owner
      or claimed mode: run no workspace gates or required validation commands
      and attach no `no-diff.json` or workspace validation logs. Run only
      commands this brief requires and retain its evidence artifacts.
    - If area reviews from an earlier full review are still open, do not file a
      second set. Record their IDs in the execution summary and finish.

    Fetch the workspace's integration branch and record the full 40-character
    SHA of its tip. Every area task names this SHA; reviewers read the tree as it
    stands there, so later merges cannot shift an area under them.

    The area bound is **25,000 tracked text lines**, a maximum, not a target
    that may be exceeded. Inventory tracked files with `git ls-tree -r -z
    <sha>` and count each text blob at that SHA (`git show <sha>:<path>`),
    including an unterminated final line. Do not measure the moving checkout
    or count a concatenated archive containing binary files. Include source,
    tests, documentation and authored assets, including files at the root.
    Vendored, generated, binary and lockfile-only content may be excluded;
    record every excluded path and its reason.

    Start with package/crate directories. Recursively split every candidate
    above 25,000 lines into disjoint child directories, keeping files directly
    in the parent as separate candidates. If a leaf directory is still too
    large, split it into disjoint file sets. Prefer module boundaries where
    they fit the bound; the bound takes precedence. Group small, closely
    related candidates only when their combined count stays within the bound.

    for whole directories and `file:` selectors for direct files or file sets;
    never select an entire parent alongside its children in different areas.
    If a single included file exceeds 25,000 lines and this rule cannot produce
    bounded areas, report `review_incomplete` with that uncovered path and
    count; do not file an oversized chore or silently exclude the file.

    inventories for gaps and duplicates. Write `.orbit/tmp/full-review-areas.json`
    with `schema_version: 1`, `pinned_sha`, `area_line_bound: 25000`, the areas
    (name, selectors, file paths and per-file counts, total line count), and
    exclusions (path and reason). Attach it to this coordinator task with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/full-review-areas.json","path":"full-review-areas.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.

    ## File one area review per area

    Title each task `Full review: <area name> @ <short SHA>`. Its description
    carries the brief below, with the pinned SHA, area's selectors, measured
    line count and complete file inventory filled in. Set `context_files` to
    those `dir:` / `file:` selectors. Use `hard`
    for areas holding concurrency, persistence, security boundaries or process
    control, and `medium` otherwise.

    Area brief:

    > Review `<area selectors>` in full as it stands at commit `<full SHA>` on
    > `<integration branch>`. This area has `<measured line count>` tracked
    > text lines (maximum 25,000); its complete file inventory and per-file
    > counts are `<inventory>`. Read the whole area, not a diff; read from that
    > commit (`git show <sha>:<path>`) if the checkout has moved.
    >
    > Before reading, list this area's task artifacts with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","field":"artifacts","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > If `read-progress.json` exists, retrieve it with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","path":"read-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > A resumed or re-crewed run must continue from that artifact, preserving
    > completed partitions and findings already filed, instead of starting
    > over. Verify its pinned SHA, area selectors and complete file/range
    > inventory match this task. A present but unreadable or mismatched artifact
    > is `review_incomplete`; do not overwrite it or pretend this is a new run.
    >
    > On the first run, divide the inventory into stable named read partitions
    > of **at most 10,000 lines** each. Prefer directory/module boundaries;
    > split files larger than a partition into explicit inclusive line ranges.
    > Cover every included line exactly once, with no gaps or overlaps, and
    > include empty files in the inventory. Read every partition in full.
    > Use parallel read passes or subagents when the crew and execution rules
    > support them; otherwise read partitions sequentially. The reviewer remains
    > responsible for reconciling every partition and checking calls and
    > invariants across their boundaries. A search, summary, sampled read or
    > truncated tool response does not count as a full read; continue in chunks
    > until all lines in the partition have been examined.
    >
    > Write `.orbit/tmp/read-progress.json` with `schema_version: 1`,
    > `pinned_sha`, `area_selectors`, `area_line_count`,
    > `partition_line_bound: 10000`, and `partitions`. Each partition records
    > its stable ID, files / inclusive line ranges, line count, status
    > (`pending`, `in_progress`, or `complete`), the ranges actually read,
    > confirmed findings with filed task IDs, and remaining checks across
    > partition boundaries. Attach the initial inventory before reading and
    > update it after each read chunk, completed partition and filed finding
    > with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/read-progress.json","path":"read-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.

    > they must not overwrite the shared artifact independently. On resume,
    > keep completed partitions, finish only unread ranges and unresolved
    > checks, and reconcile the artifact before claiming full coverage.
    >
    > Look for:
    > - correctness: logic errors, wrong edge cases, broken invariants between
    >   callers and callees;
    > - error handling: swallowed or mislabelled errors, panics reachable from
    >   input, partial writes left behind on failure;
    > - concurrency: races, lock ordering, locks held across awaits, unbounded
    >   or leaked tasks;
    > - security boundaries: path traversal, injection, trust of unvalidated
    >   input, secrets in logs or output;
    > - resource bounds: unbounded buffers, queues, retries, recursion or file
    >   growth;
    > - conformance to the repository's documented standards: its agent guide,
    >   contributing guide, standards documents and lint configuration;
    > - tests that do not test what they claim: assertions that cannot fail,
    >   fixtures that bypass the code under test, names that promise behavior
    >   the body never exercises.
    >
    > Verify every candidate against the code at the pinned SHA; a line that
    > looks wrong but is guarded elsewhere is not a finding. Before filing,
    > search for existing coverage with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<distinctive symptom, symbol, or file terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    > and skip anything an open `code-review` task already tracks. File each
    > confirmed finding as its own task with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["code-review","full-code-review"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
    > citing `file:line` evidence at the pinned SHA. Derive canonical `file:`
    > selectors from every evidenced source path, removing the line suffix,
    > and add the matching regression-test location. Use existing paths where
    > possible; for a test file that must be created, set
    > `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that intended path. Never file
    > a finding without context selectors. Skip nitpicks.
    > When the finding is a regression a landed task introduced (squash-merge
    > subjects carry its ID as `[<task-id>]`; confirm with `orbit.task.show`), add
    > `{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>","regression":{"nature":"<nature>","escape":"<escape>"}}`
    > to its `relations` and name the culprit commit in its description. A
    > claimed run cannot record that relation: name the culprit, nature and escape
    > in the description instead. Never blame a bystander task.
    > Choose `unclassified` rather than guess. `nature` is what kind of regression
    > the link records:
    > - `broke_existing`: the culprit broke behavior that worked before it landed.
    > - `defect_in_new`: the defect is in code the culprit itself introduced.
    > - `incomplete`: the culprit shipped without part of what its task required.
    > - `merge_reintroduced`: a merge restored code or assets an earlier change had removed.
    > - `contract_drift`: docs, schemas or a contract drifted from the behavior the culprit shipped.
    > - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the nature.
    > `escape` is why the delivery gates missed it:
    > - `no_test`: no test covered the broken behavior.
    > - `test_not_selected`: a covering test existed but the delivery's gates did not run it.
    > - `platform_only`: it shows only on a platform or host the gates did not exercise.
    > - `review_missed`: it was visible in the diff and review did not flag it.
    > - `spec_ambiguous`: the task or spec left the expected behavior open to the shipped reading.
    > - `nondeterministic`: it depends on timing, ordering or environment and passed when gated.
    > - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the escape.
    >
    > If full reading or a partition bound cannot be met, attach the latest
    > progress and return `result.blocker` with `kind: review_incomplete` and
    > evidence naming each uncovered partition, file / unread line range and
    > unresolved check. Put the same inventory in the task comment (return
    > `comment` in claimed mode) so it remains visible on the blocked task;
    > leave lifecycle transitions to the pipeline. Incomplete reading is never
    > a clean no-op. Only an area with every partition fully read, checks across
    > partitions resolved and no confirmed findings is a successful no-op.
    > This `no-diff-expected` review runs no workspace gates or required
    > validation commands and attaches no `no-diff.json` or workspace
    > validation logs, in owner or claimed mode. Run only commands this brief
    > requires and retain the reading and finding evidence above.
    > Record the SHA, area line count, per-partition coverage, progress artifact
    > and each filed task ID in the execution summary.

    Give each area task these acceptance criteria: the whole area was read at
    the pinned SHA using partitions of at most 10,000 lines, with complete
    per-partition coverage in `read-progress.json` and resumed runs continuing
    from it; every filed finding is verified, non-duplicate, a `bug`
    tagged `code-review` and `full-code-review` with `file:line` evidence at
    that SHA and source/test context selectors; a fully read clean area succeeds
    as a no-op, while incomplete reading reports uncovered partitions in the
    progress artifact and task comment with `review_incomplete`.

    ## Finish

    Finish once every area task is filed. Record in the execution summary the
    integration branch and pinned SHA, the area table (area name, directories,
    measured line count, complexity) with any exclusions, and each area's task
    ID.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - One integration-branch commit was pinned by full SHA and every area task names it.
  - The tracked tree is partitioned into areas of at most 25,000 text lines along directory or file boundaries, with measured inventories in `full-review-areas.json` and every exclusion named; an unpartitionable oversized file is reported as `review_incomplete`, never filed as an oversized area.
  - Each bounded area has exactly one filed `chore` tagged `full-code-review` and `no-diff-expected` (never `code-review`), complexity `hard` at most, no crew, source `dir:` / `file:` context selectors, artifact read/write tools, a measured line count, the partitioned reading and resume brief, and a `spawned_from` relation to this task.
  - The execution summary records the pinned SHA, the area table and every area task ID.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - full-code-review
  - no-diff-expected
  required_tools:
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.list
  - orbit.task.artifact.put
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  status: backlog

    for whole directories and `file:` selectors for direct files or file sets;
    never select an entire parent alongside its children in different areas.
    If a single included file exceeds 25,000 lines and this rule cannot produce
    bounded areas, report `review_incomplete` with that uncovered path and
    count; do not file an oversized chore or silently exclude the file.

    Before filing, verify all area counts against the bound and reconcile the
    inventories for gaps and duplicates. Write `.orbit/tmp/review-areas.json`
    with `schema_version: 1`, `pinned_sha`, `area_line_bound: 25000`, the areas
    (name, selectors, file paths and per-file counts, total line count), and
    exclusions (path and reason). Attach it to this coordinator task with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/review-areas.json","path":"review-areas.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.

    ## File one area review per area

    Title each task `Full review: <area name> @ <short SHA>`. Its description
    carries the brief below, with the pinned SHA, area's selectors, measured
    line count and complete file inventory filled in. Set `context_files` to
    those `dir:` / `file:` selectors. Use `hard`
    for areas holding concurrency, persistence, security boundaries or process
    control, and `medium` otherwise.

    Area brief:

    > Review `<area selectors>` in full as it stands at commit `<full SHA>` on
    > `<integration branch>`. This area has `<measured line count>` tracked
    > text lines (maximum 25,000); its complete file inventory and per-file
    > counts are `<inventory>`. Read the whole area, not a diff; read from that
    > commit (`git show <sha>:<path>`) if the checkout has moved.
    >
    > Before reading, list this area's task artifacts with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","field":"artifacts","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > If `read-progress.json` exists, retrieve it with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","path":"read-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > A resumed or re-crewed run must continue from that artifact, preserving
    > completed partitions and findings already filed, instead of starting
    > over. Verify its pinned SHA, area selectors and complete file/range
    > inventory match this task. A present but unreadable or mismatched artifact
    > is `review_incomplete`; do not overwrite it or pretend this is a new run.
    >
    > On the first run, divide the inventory into stable named read partitions
    > of **at most 10,000 lines** each. Prefer directory/module boundaries;
    > split files larger than a partition into explicit inclusive line ranges.
    > Cover every included line exactly once, with no gaps or overlaps, and
    > include empty files in the inventory. Read every partition in full.
    > Use parallel read passes or subagents when the crew and execution rules
    > support them; otherwise read partitions sequentially. The reviewer remains
    > responsible for reconciling every partition and checking calls and
    > invariants across their boundaries. A search, summary, sampled read or
    > truncated tool response does not count as a full read; continue in chunks
    > until all lines in the partition have been examined.
    >
    > Write `.orbit/tmp/read-progress.json` with `schema_version: 1`,
    > `pinned_sha`, `area_selectors`, `area_line_count`,
    > `partition_line_bound: 10000`, and `partitions`. Each partition records
    > its stable ID, files / inclusive line ranges, line count, status
    > (`pending`, `in_progress`, or `complete`), the ranges actually read,
    > confirmed findings with filed task IDs, and remaining checks across
    > partition boundaries. Attach the initial inventory before reading and
    > update it after each read chunk, completed partition and filed finding
    > with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/read-progress.json","path":"read-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > Parallel readers return progress to one owner who merges and attaches it;
    > they must not overwrite the shared artifact independently. On resume,
    > keep completed partitions, finish only unread ranges and unresolved
    > checks, and reconcile the artifact before claiming full coverage.
    >
    > Look for:
    > - correctness: logic errors, wrong edge cases, broken invariants between
    >   callers and callees;
    > - error handling: swallowed or mislabelled errors, panics reachable from
    >   input, partial writes left behind on failure;
    > - concurrency: races, lock ordering, locks held across awaits, unbounded
    >   or leaked tasks;
    > - security boundaries: path traversal, injection, trust of unvalidated
    >   input, secrets in logs or output;
    > - resource bounds: unbounded buffers, queues, retries, recursion or file
    >   growth;
    > - conformance to the repository's documented standards: its agent guide,
    >   contributing guide, standards documents and lint configuration;
    > - tests that do not test what they claim: assertions that cannot fail,
    >   fixtures that bypass the code under test, names that promise behavior
    >   the body never exercises.
    >
    > Verify every candidate against the code at the pinned SHA; a line that
    > looks wrong but is guarded elsewhere is not a finding. Before filing,
    > search for existing coverage with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<distinctive symptom, symbol, or file terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    > and skip anything an open `code-review` task already tracks. File each
    > confirmed finding as its own task with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["code-review","full-code-review"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
    > citing `file:line` evidence at the pinned SHA. Derive canonical `file:`
    > selectors from every evidenced source path, removing the line suffix,
    > and add the matching regression-test location. Use existing paths where
    > possible; for a test file that must be created, set
    > `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that intended path. Never file
    > a finding without context selectors. Skip nitpicks.
    >
    > If full reading or a partition bound cannot be met, attach the latest
    > progress and return `result.blocker` with `kind: review_incomplete` and
    > evidence naming each uncovered partition, file / unread line range and
    > unresolved check. Put the same inventory in the task comment (return
    > `comment` in claimed mode) so it remains visible on the blocked task;
    > leave lifecycle transitions to the pipeline. Incomplete reading is never
    > a clean no-op. Only an area with every partition fully read, checks across
    > partitions resolved and no confirmed findings is a successful no-op;
    > follow the workspace's no-diff artifact and validation requirements.
    > Record the SHA, area line count, per-partition coverage, progress artifact
    > and each filed task ID in the execution summary.

    Give each area task these acceptance criteria: the whole area was read at
    the pinned SHA using partitions of at most 10,000 lines, with complete
    per-partition coverage in `read-progress.json` and resumed runs continuing
    from it; every filed finding is verified, non-duplicate, a `bug`
    tagged `code-review` and `full-code-review` with `file:line` evidence at
    that SHA and source/test context selectors; a fully read clean area succeeds
    as a no-op, while incomplete reading reports uncovered partitions in the
    progress artifact and task comment with `review_incomplete`.

    ## Finish

    Finish once every area task is filed. Record in the execution summary the
    integration branch and pinned SHA, the area table (area name, directories,
    measured line count, complexity) with any exclusions, and each area's task
    ID.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - One integration-branch commit was pinned by full SHA and every area task names it.
  - The tracked tree is partitioned into areas of at most 25,000 text lines along directory or file boundaries, with measured inventories in `review-areas.json` and every exclusion named; an unpartitionable oversized file is reported as `review_incomplete`, never filed as an oversized area.
  - Each bounded area has exactly one filed `chore` tagged `full-code-review` and `no-diff-expected` (never `code-review`), complexity `hard` at most, no crew, source `dir:` / `file:` context selectors, artifact read/write tools, a measured line count, the partitioned reading and resume brief, and a `spawned_from` relation to this task.
  - The execution summary records the pinned SHA, the area table and every area task ID.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - full-code-review
  - no-diff-expected
  required_tools:
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.list
  - orbit.task.artifact.put
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  # The portable system lane is seeded per machine and compatibility-aliased
  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog
dedupe: skip_if_open
