      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"<medium|hard>","type":"chore","tags":["qa-full-sweep","no-diff-expected"],"context_files":["dir:<source or documentation directory implementing the area>"],"required_tools":["orbit.search","orbit.task.add","orbit.task.show","orbit.task.artifact.get","orbit.task.artifact.put"],"relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"priority":"medium","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      File the roll-up task with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"low","type":"chore","tags":["qa-full-sweep","qa-full-sweep-rollup","no-diff-expected","auto-task:qa-full-sweep"],"required_tools":["orbit.task.show","orbit.task.artifact.get","orbit.task.artifact.put"],"relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"priority":"medium","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Area tasks carry exactly the tags `qa-full-sweep` and `no-diff-expected`,
      complexity `hard` at most (never `xhard`), and no `crew`, so each is
      routed by automatic selection. Give the roll-up no `crew` either.
    - The roll-up carries this definition's `auto-task:qa-full-sweep`
      provenance tag on purpose: the scheduler's open-instance dedupe then
      refuses to mint another sweep until the roll-up is done, and the roll-up
      waits for every area.
    - If any task listed above other than this one is still open (area tasks
      or a roll-up from an earlier sweep), do not file a second set. Record
      their IDs in the execution summary and finish.
    - Never repair what you find, dispatch agents or jobs, release, tag,
      publish or deploy.
    - This coordinator, its area tasks and the roll-up are `no-diff-expected`,
      in owner or claimed mode: run no workspace gates or required validation
      commands and attach no `no-diff.json` or workspace validation logs.
      Run only commands their own brief requires; the area's product build
      and scenario commands remain required. Retain the brief's QA evidence.

    ## Pin the commit

    Fetch the workspace's integration branch and record the full 40-character
    SHA of its tip. Every area task and the roll-up name this SHA; testers
    build and run the product as it stands there, so later merges cannot shift
    an area under them.

    ## Inventory the user-facing surface

    If the repository ships its own full-QA runbook, scenario inventory or
    harness, use it as the inventory and command source instead of deriving
    one, and record which files you used. Otherwise derive the inventory from
    the repository's own documentation and entry points at the pinned SHA:
    the README, setup, install and run instructions, command-line help trees
    (run `--help` on every command and subcommand of the built product),
    HTTP or RPC API routes, UI pages, configuration surfaces and documented
    workflows. List the surface as a user meets it, not as the source tree
    is laid out.

    For each surface record the scenarios a user depends on: the normal path,
    failure and recovery paths, and boundary inputs. Mark each scenario
    `required` unless the repository documents it as optional, and name any
    capability it needs beyond a local build (authentication, an external
    provider, a specific operating system, a browser, network access, or
    public post-release state). Internal-only code with no user-facing entry
    point, generated or vendored content, and surfaces the repository marks
    deprecated may be excluded; record every exclusion and its reason.

    ## Partition into bounded areas

    Group the inventory into areas, each one coherent user-facing surface (one
    command group, one API resource family, one UI section or one documented
    workflow) holding **at most 20 required scenarios**. Split a larger
    surface into smaller coherent parts; group small related surfaces only
    when the result stays within the bound. Every inventoried scenario belongs
    to exactly one area.

    Write `.orbit/tmp/qa-full-sweep-inventory.json` with `schema_version: 1`,
    `pinned_sha`, `integration_branch`, `sources` (the documents, entry points
    or shipped harness the inventory came from), `areas` (each with `name`,
    `surface`, `boundaries` exercised, `context_files`, and `scenarios`, each
    scenario with `id`, `description`, `required` and `capabilities`) and
    `exclusions` (each with the excluded surface and its `reason`). Attach it
    to this coordinator task with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/qa-full-sweep-inventory.json","path":"qa-full-sweep-inventory.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    After filing, add each area's `task_id` and the `rollup_task_id` to the
    file and attach it again under the same name.

    ## File one surface-QA task per area

    Title each task `Full QA: <area name> @ <short SHA>`. Its description
    carries the area brief below with the pinned SHA, integration branch, area
    name, surface, boundaries and complete scenario list filled in. Set
    `context_files` to the `dir:` / `file:` selectors of the source and
    documentation that implement the area; the tester modifies none of them.
    Use `hard` for areas that need isolated services, concurrency, persistence
    or destructive operations, and `medium` otherwise.

    Area brief:

    > QA `<area name>` (`<surface>`) of this product as it stands at commit
    > `<full SHA>` on `<integration branch>`, through its real boundaries
    > (`<boundaries>`). The required scenarios are `<scenario list>`. This is
    > a leaf QA mandate: never repair what you find, dispatch agents or jobs,
    > release, tag, publish or deploy.
    >
    > Before starting, list this area's task artifacts with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","field":"artifacts","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > If `qa-progress.json` exists, retrieve it with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","path":"qa-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > A resumed or re-crewed run continues from that artifact, keeping every
    > recorded outcome and filed finding, instead of starting over. Verify its
    > pinned SHA, area and scenario list match this task. A present but
    > unreadable or mismatched artifact is `qa_incomplete`; do not overwrite
    > it or pretend this is a new run.
    >
    > Build the candidate at the pinned SHA by following the repository's own
    > build and run instructions. Exercise each scenario as a user would,
    > through the product's real command line, API, UI or documented workflow,
    > covering the normal path, failure and recovery, and boundary inputs.
    > Re-running the test suite is not QA: a passing suite is supporting
    > evidence at most, never a scenario result.
    >
    > Run anything that writes state against isolated, disposable roots,
    > workspaces, accounts and repositories created for this run. Never use
    > the product's live data root, the real task store or the operator's own
    > configuration. In agent-executor sandboxes and linked job-run worktrees
    > the managed `.git` mount is read-only by design; do not work around it
    > by chmod or host-side gitdir writes. To build a revision other than the
    > checkout, extract it to a writable scratch directory with
    > `mkdir -p .orbit/tmp/qa-base && git archive <sha> | tar -x -C .orbit/tmp/qa-base`.
    > Restore a modified tracked file with `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`
    > when `git checkout --` cannot take `index.lock`, and run read-only git
    > inspection with `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`. Put build caches and scratch
    > state in a writable scratch location sized for the build, never the
    > machine's real home directory. Confirm every long build or command by a
    > positive completion marker in its captured output (the tool's own final
    > summary line); its absence means "did not run" regardless of the exit
    > status.
    >
    > Prepare capabilities before marking a browser or website scenario unrun.
    > When the host's browser kit is verified, your environment carries
    > `ORBIT_BROWSER_KIT_ENV`: source it in the worker shell and use its
    > `PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE` and `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`. Also forward
    > `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `FONTCONFIG_FILE` on Linux when it sets them;
    > macOS needs no Linux loader or font inputs. Read the shared kit without
    > modifying it, and never run `orbit browser-kit` from the worker. When
    > the variable is absent, record `orbit browser-kit install` as the host
    > fix in the capability probe. If no kit is usable, use the repository's
    > disposable Playwright/Chromium recipe under `.orbit/tmp/` (for this
    > repository, docs/runbooks/website-validation.md), unpacking missing
    > Linux libraries without root. Do not install host packages or bypass
    > the worker sandbox. A genuinely unavailable path or failed Chromium
    > launch remains `NOT_RUN` with the capability probe retained.
    >
    > For repositories with `scripts/qa-full-sweep.sh`, pass the sourced kit
    > explicitly: `--playwright-module "$PLAYWRIGHT_MODULE"`,
    > `--playwright-browsers-path "$PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH"`, and, when
    > nonempty, `--browser-ld-library-path "$LD_LIBRARY_PATH"` and
    > `--browser-fontconfig-file "$FONTCONFIG_FILE"`. Preserve a
    > colon-separated library search path as one quoted argument. Retain
    > the launched Chromium version and screenshots with
    > `--browser-evidence-dir .orbit/tmp/qa-full-sweep/browser`. Follow
    > docs/runbooks/qa-full-sweep.md for the full invocation and disposable
    > fallback paths. Include `--website-build --run-commands`: the website
    > leg prepares dependencies with `npm ci` and a private npm cache in a
    > scratch source copy through the isolated procedure in
    > docs/runbooks/website-validation.md, then builds and records `PASS`
    > or `FAIL`. It never deploys. For other repositories, use their own
    > isolated dependency preparation and build commands.
    >
    > Write `.orbit/tmp/qa-progress.json` with `schema_version: 1`,
    > `pinned_sha`, `area`, `candidate` (how the build was made and its
    > identity) and `scenarios`. Each scenario records its `id`, `required`,
    > `boundary`, the exact `command` or steps, an `outcome` of `PASS`,
    > `FAIL`, `BLOCKED` or `NOT_RUN`, its `evidence` (captured output or a
    > log artifact name), any `missing_capability`, and the `finding_task_id`
    > for a filed failure. Attach it before the first scenario and again after
    > each scenario and each filed finding with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/qa-progress.json","path":"qa-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > Attach referenced logs the same way.
    >
    > A scenario that needs a capability this run lacks (authentication, an
    > external provider, another operating system, a browser, network access
    > or public post-release state) is `BLOCKED` or `NOT_RUN` with the missing
    > capability named, never `PASS`. Evidence from one operating system does
    > not verify another. A command that exits zero without the behaviour the
    > scenario requires is `FAIL`, not `PASS`.
    >
    > For every `FAIL`, search open and closed tasks before filing with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<scenario, exact error and boundary terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > Reuse an open task whose reproducer covers the same defect, and reassess
    > a closed one against the pinned SHA rather than treating it as
    > suppression. File each confirmed non-duplicate finding as its own task with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["qa-full-sweep"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > Its description holds the exact reproducer, the pinned SHA, the
    > environment, expected and observed results and the evidence artifact.
    > Derive canonical `file:` selectors from the source that implements the
    > failing behaviour and add the matching regression-test location. Use
    > existing paths where possible; for a test file that must be created,
    > set `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that intended path.
    > Never file a finding without context selectors. Record each finding's
    > task ID on its scenario.
    >
    > Finish only when every scenario has a recorded outcome; recording a
    > `FAIL`, `BLOCKED` or `NOT_RUN` honestly completes this task, and the
    > sweep's roll-up turns it into the release decision. If the run cannot
    > record every scenario, attach the latest progress and return
    > `result.blocker` with `kind: qa_incomplete` and evidence naming each
    > unrecorded scenario. Put the same list in the task comment (return
    > `comment` in claimed mode) and leave lifecycle transitions to the
    > pipeline. This `no-diff-expected` area runs no workspace gates or required
    > validation commands and attaches no `no-diff.json` or workspace
    > validation logs, in owner or claimed mode. Run only commands this brief
    > requires, including the product build and scenarios; retain their QA
    > evidence. A completed area leaves the repository unchanged. Record the
    > SHA, candidate identity, per-scenario outcomes, the progress artifact
    > and each filed task ID in the execution summary.

    Give each area task these acceptance criteria: the candidate was built at
    the pinned SHA and every scenario was exercised through the product's real
    boundaries in isolated disposable roots; every scenario has a PASS, FAIL,
    BLOCKED or NOT_RUN outcome with its command and evidence in
    `qa-progress.json`, and resumed runs continued from it; no
    capability-gated scenario is recorded as PASS; every failure maps to a
    verified, non-duplicate `bug` tagged `qa-full-sweep` with a reproducer,
    the pinned SHA and source/test context selectors, or to an existing task
    that already covers it.

    ## File the roll-up

    After every area task is filed, file one roll-up task titled
    `Full QA decision @ <short SHA>`. Its description carries the roll-up
    brief below with the pinned SHA, integration branch and the area table
    (area name and task ID) filled in. Then make it wait for every area by
    setting its dependencies with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.update --input '{"id":"<roll-up task ID>","dependencies":["<area task ID>"],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
    listing every area task ID. When `orbit.task.update` is unavailable (in
    claimed mode), record in the returned `comment` that the roll-up's
    dependencies must be set to the listed area IDs.

    Roll-up brief:

    > Decide the full QA sweep of commit `<full SHA>` on
    > `<integration branch>` from its areas `<area table>`. File nothing,
    > repair nothing, dispatch nothing.
    >
    > First confirm with `orbit.task.show` that every listed area task is
    > `done`. If any is not, do not decide: return `result.blocker` with
    > `kind: qa_areas_open` naming the open areas.
    >
    > For each area, retrieve its `qa-progress.json` with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<area task ID>","path":"qa-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > An area whose artifact is missing, unreadable, names another SHA or
    > area, or leaves a listed scenario without an outcome counts as
    > incomplete.
    >
    > The decision is `PASS` only when every area is complete and every
    > required scenario in every area is `PASS`. Any required `FAIL`,
    > `BLOCKED` or `NOT_RUN`, or any incomplete area, makes it `INCOMPLETE`.
    > Write `.orbit/tmp/qa-full-sweep-decision.json` with `schema_version: 1`,
    > `pinned_sha`, `decision`, and per area its task ID, the count of
    > required scenarios by outcome, and every non-`PASS` required scenario
    > with its outcome and finding task ID. Attach it with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this roll-up task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/qa-full-sweep-decision.json","path":"qa-full-sweep-decision.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > Then record the swept commit as this task's cursor:
    > write `{"schema_version":1,"ref":"<integration branch>","cursor":"<full SHA>"}`
    > to `.orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json` and attach it as `sweep-cursor.json`
    > the same way, so the scheduler skips the next tick when nothing has
    > landed since. Record the decision, the per-area table and the
    > non-`PASS` scenarios in the execution summary.

    Give the roll-up these acceptance criteria: every area task was `done`
    before the decision; `qa-full-sweep-decision.json` records `PASS` only
    when every required scenario in every area passed, and `INCOMPLETE`
    otherwise, with each non-`PASS` required scenario named;
    `sweep-cursor.json` records the pinned SHA.

    ## Finish

    Finish once every area task and the roll-up are filed and the roll-up's
    dependencies are set. Record in the execution summary the integration
    branch and pinned SHA, the inventory source, the area table (area name,
    surface, required scenario count, complexity, task ID) with any
    exclusions, and the roll-up task ID.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - One integration-branch commit was pinned by full SHA and every area task and the roll-up name it.
  - '`qa-full-sweep-inventory.json` is attached to this task with `schema_version`, `pinned_sha`, the areas and their scenarios, and every exclusion with its reason; each area holds at most 20 required scenarios.'
  - Each area has exactly one filed `chore` tagged `qa-full-sweep` and `no-diff-expected`, complexity `hard` at most, no crew, source or documentation context selectors, a `spawned_from` relation to this task, and the hands-on area brief.
  - One roll-up chore tagged `qa-full-sweep`, `qa-full-sweep-rollup`, `no-diff-expected` and `auto-task:qa-full-sweep` was filed with a `spawned_from` relation to this task and dependencies on every area task.
  - When tasks from an earlier sweep were still open, no new area tasks or roll-up were filed and their IDs are in the execution summary.
  - The execution summary records the pinned SHA, the area table with every area task ID, the exclusions and the roll-up task ID.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - qa-full-sweep
  - no-diff-expected
  required_tools:
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.list
  - orbit.task.update
  - orbit.task.artifact.put
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  status: backlog
dedupe: skip_if_open
skip_if_unchanged:
  ref: __ORBIT_BASE_BRANCH__
  cursor:
    tags:
    - qa-full-sweep
    - qa-full-sweep-rollup
    - auto-task:qa-full-sweep

qa-sweep.00e37d84bbcaea1ef712602bc2bfd99602151f6f:
schemaVersion: 1
name: qa-sweep
description: Hands-on validation of recent workspace changes
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 50 * * * *
template:
  title: Perform QA validation
  description: |
    Identify recent changes in this workspace and validate them hands-on. Build
    and run the changed software, then exercise the affected CLI, API, and
    feature paths as a user would; do not treat re-running the existing test
    suite as sufficient validation.

    Follow this repository's documented setup and run instructions. When a
    sandbox or other environment constraint makes the usual local state
    unwritable, put scratch checkouts, caches, and other ephemeral state in a
    writable temporary location rather than the machine's real home directory
    or the product's live data root. A writable temporary location may be too
    small for build output; choose the build cache location for capacity.

    In agent-executor sandboxes and linked job-run worktrees, the repository's
    managed `.git` mount is read-only by design and must not be worked around by
    chmod or host-side gitdir writes. Because `.git` is read-only, commands that
    attempt write access to `.git` fail (such as `git worktree add` or `git checkout --`).
    Instead:
    - To build an arbitrary baseline revision without writing `.git` or creating
      `.git/worktrees/*`, extract an archive to a writable scratch directory:
      `mkdir -p /tmp/base && git archive <sha> | tar -x -C /tmp/base`,
      then build there using a dedicated build cache/target directory.
    - To revert a modified tracked file when `git checkout -- <path>` fails
      because it cannot acquire `index.lock`, restore it from the commit tree:
      `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`.
    - Read-only inspection commands such as `git status --short` succeed with
      `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

    A long build or test command's completion must be confirmed by a positive
    marker in its captured output (`test result:`, `Finished`, or the target's
    own final line), with its absence treated as "did not run" regardless of the
    reported exit status.

    Before reporting anything, search the workspace's configured task or issue surface
    for open work covering the same problem. File each confirmed finding with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["qa-sweep"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Give it severity-appropriate priority and put the relevant commits, observed
    evidence, and exact reproduction steps in its description. Derive canonical
    `file:` selectors from every evidenced source path, removing the line suffix,
    and add the matching regression-test location. Use existing paths where
    possible; for a test file that must be created, set
    `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that intended path. Never file a
    finding without context selectors. Skip duplicates.

    A non-duplicate failing test that blocks the repository's
    standard validation command must be filed as a durable issue even when
    the failure is sandbox-specific, platform-specific, or otherwise
    environment-specific, including test-harness or portability defects.
    Do not leave such a breaking test in narrative-only output. Distinguish
    clearly between validation impact (the prescribed suite cannot complete)
    and production impact (whether the failure demonstrates a production
    defect). Include the failing command, the exact error, relevant
    environment evidence, and a scope assessment.

    ## Record the cursor

    Record the candidate revision you validated as this task's machine-readable
    cursor artifact, `sweep-cursor.json`, which the scheduler reads to decide
    whether the next tick has anything left to validate. Its exact content is
    `{"schema_version":1,"ref":"<integration branch>","cursor":"<full 40-character commit SHA>"}`;
    write it to `.orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json` and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json","path":"sweep-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    `orbit tool show <tool.name>` prints the tool's schema. Write it on every
    completed sweep, including one that found nothing to fix — a sweep without
    it leaves the next tick no cursor to compare the branch tip against.

    Your narrative output is advisory; the issues you file are the durable
    side-effect channel.

    ## Persist the execution summary

    In an ordinary managed activity, persist a meaningful `execution_summary`
    on this task with `orbit.task.update` before finishing. Include the
    validated revision, each command run with a passed, failed, or not-run
    outcome, any coverage gaps, and the filed task IDs; when no issues were
    found, state "no repository changes". A successful agent response does not
    substitute for persisting this task field.

    In claimed mode, `orbit.task.update` is unavailable. Return the same
    execution summary in the output so the owner can import it.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Recent changes were exercised through their real user-facing paths.
  - Real, non-duplicate issues were filed on the workspace's configured task or issue surface with evidence and reproduction steps.
  - The validated candidate revision is attached as this task's `sweep-cursor.json` artifact (`schema_version` 1, the integration branch, and the full commit SHA).
  - Non-duplicate failing tests that block the prescribed validation command were filed as durable issues, with validation impact distinguished from production impact.
  - The persisted execution summary, or the returned summary for owner import in claimed mode, records the validated revision, commands run with passed/failed/not-run outcomes, coverage gaps, and filed task IDs or "no repository changes" when none were found.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - qa-sweep
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  # The portable system lane is seeded per machine and compatibility-aliased
  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog
dedupe: skip_if_open
skip_if_unchanged:
  ref: __ORBIT_BASE_BRANCH__
  cursor:
    tags:
    - qa-sweep
    - no-diff-expected

qa-sweep.37d10744d68d076be18ace14b3387d9f961da570:
schemaVersion: 1
name: qa-sweep
description: Hands-on validation of recent workspace changes
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 50 * * * *
template:
  title: Perform QA validation
  description: |
    Identify recent changes in this workspace and validate them hands-on. Build
    and run the changed software, then exercise the affected CLI, API, and
    feature paths as a user would; do not treat re-running the existing test
    suite as sufficient validation.

    Follow this repository's documented setup and run instructions. When a
    sandbox or other environment constraint makes the usual local state
    unwritable, put scratch checkouts, caches, and other ephemeral state in a
    writable temporary location rather than the machine's real home directory
    or the product's live data root. A writable temporary location may be too
    small for build output; choose the build cache location for capacity.

    In agent-executor sandboxes and linked job-run worktrees, the repository's
    managed `.git` mount is read-only by design and must not be worked around by
    chmod or host-side gitdir writes. Because `.git` is read-only, commands that
    attempt write access to `.git` fail (such as `git worktree add` or `git checkout --`).
    Instead:
    - To build an arbitrary baseline revision without writing `.git` or creating
      `.git/worktrees/*`, extract an archive to a writable scratch directory:
      `mkdir -p /tmp/base && git archive <sha> | tar -x -C /tmp/base`,
      then build there using a dedicated build cache/target directory.
    - To revert a modified tracked file when `git checkout -- <path>` fails
      because it cannot acquire `index.lock`, restore it from the commit tree:
      `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`.
    - Read-only inspection commands such as `git status --short` succeed with
      `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

    A long build or test command's completion must be confirmed by a positive
    marker in its captured output (`test result:`, `Finished`, or the target's
    own final line), with its absence treated as "did not run" regardless of the
    reported exit status.

    Before reporting anything, search the workspace's configured task or issue surface
    for open work covering the same problem. File each confirmed finding with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["qa-sweep"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Give it severity-appropriate priority and put the relevant commits, observed
    evidence, and exact reproduction steps in its description. Derive canonical
    `file:` selectors from every evidenced source path, removing the line suffix,
    and add the matching regression-test location. Use existing paths where
    possible; for a test file that must be created, set
    `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that intended path. Never file a
    finding without context selectors. Skip duplicates. Add `ui` to the tags
    of a finding in something a user sees (dashboard, web pages, docs site,
    desktop app UI), and attach its screenshot to the filed task with
    `orbit.task.artifact.put` at a stable path such as
    `screenshots/<view>-<theme>-<width>.png`, under the 1 MiB artifact limit:
    `.orbit/tmp/` is cleared with the worktree.

    When the finding is a regression a landed task introduced (squash-merge
    subjects carry its ID as `[<task-id>]`; confirm with `orbit.task.show`), add
    `{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>","regression":{"nature":"<nature>","escape":"<escape>"}}`
    to its `relations` and name the culprit commit in its description. A
    claimed run cannot record that relation: name the culprit, nature and escape
    in the description instead. Never blame a bystander task.
    Choose `unclassified` rather than guess. `nature` is what kind of regression
    the link records:
    - `broke_existing`: the culprit broke behavior that worked before it landed.
    - `defect_in_new`: the defect is in code the culprit itself introduced.
    - `incomplete`: the culprit shipped without part of what its task required.
    - `merge_reintroduced`: a merge restored code or assets an earlier change had removed.
    - `contract_drift`: docs, schemas or a contract drifted from the behavior the culprit shipped.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the nature.
    `escape` is why the delivery gates missed it:
    - `no_test`: no test covered the broken behavior.
    - `test_not_selected`: a covering test existed but the delivery's gates did not run it.
    - `platform_only`: it shows only on a platform or host the gates did not exercise.
    - `review_missed`: it was visible in the diff and review did not flag it.
    - `spec_ambiguous`: the task or spec left the expected behavior open to the shipped reading.
    - `nondeterministic`: it depends on timing, ordering or environment and passed when gated.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the escape.

    A non-duplicate failing test that blocks the repository's
    standard validation command must be filed as a durable issue even when
    the failure is sandbox-specific, platform-specific, or otherwise
    environment-specific, including test-harness or portability defects.
    Do not leave such a breaking test in narrative-only output. Distinguish
    clearly between validation impact (the prescribed suite cannot complete)
    and production impact (whether the failure demonstrates a production
    defect). Include the failing command, the exact error, relevant
    environment evidence, and a scope assessment.

    ## Record the cursor

    Record the candidate revision you validated as this task's machine-readable
    cursor artifact, `sweep-cursor.json`, which the scheduler reads to decide
    whether the next tick has anything left to validate. Its exact content is
    `{"schema_version":1,"ref":"<integration branch>","cursor":"<full 40-character commit SHA>"}`;
    write it to `.orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json` and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json","path":"sweep-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    `orbit tool show <tool.name>` prints the tool's schema. Write it on every
    completed sweep, including one that found nothing to fix — a sweep without
    it leaves the next tick no cursor to compare the branch tip against.

    Your narrative output is advisory; the issues you file are the durable
    side-effect channel.

    ## Persist the execution summary

    In an ordinary managed activity, persist a meaningful `execution_summary`
    on this task with `orbit.task.update` before finishing. Include the
    validated revision, each command run with a passed, failed, or not-run
    outcome, any coverage gaps, and the filed task IDs; when no issues were
    found, state "no repository changes". A successful agent response does not
    substitute for persisting this task field.

    In claimed mode, `orbit.task.update` is unavailable. Return the same
    execution summary in the output so the owner can import it.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Recent changes were exercised through their real user-facing paths.
  - Real, non-duplicate issues were filed on the workspace's configured task or issue surface with evidence and reproduction steps.
  - The validated candidate revision is attached as this task's `sweep-cursor.json` artifact (`schema_version` 1, the integration branch, and the full commit SHA).
  - Non-duplicate failing tests that block the prescribed validation command were filed as durable issues, with validation impact distinguished from production impact.
  - The persisted execution summary, or the returned summary for owner import in claimed mode, records the validated revision, commands run with passed/failed/not-run outcomes, coverage gaps, and filed task IDs or "no repository changes" when none were found.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - qa-sweep
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  status: backlog
dedupe: skip_if_open
skip_if_unchanged:
  ref: __ORBIT_BASE_BRANCH__
  cursor:
    tags:
    - qa-sweep
    - no-diff-expected

schemaVersion: 1
name: qa-sweep
description: Hands-on validation of recent workspace changes
enabled: false
schedule:

template:
  title: Perform QA validation
  description: |

    and run the changed software, then exercise the affected CLI, API, and
    feature paths as a user would; do not treat re-running the existing test
    suite as sufficient validation.

    Follow this repository's documented setup and run instructions. When a
    sandbox or other environment constraint makes the usual local state
    unwritable, put scratch checkouts, caches, and other ephemeral state in a
    writable temporary location rather than the machine's real home directory
    or the product's live data root. A writable temporary location may be too
    small for build output; choose the build cache location for capacity.

    In agent-executor sandboxes and linked job-run worktrees, the repository's
    managed `.git` mount is read-only by design and must not be worked around by
    chmod or host-side gitdir writes. Because `.git` is read-only, commands that
    attempt write access to `.git` fail (such as `git worktree add` or `git checkout --`).
    Instead:
    - To build an arbitrary baseline revision without writing `.git` or creating
      `.git/worktrees/*`, extract an archive into a new, empty scratch directory:

      then `git archive <sha> | tar -x -C <that path>`. A fresh directory per
      extraction keeps files from an earlier archive out of the baseline. Then
      build there using a dedicated build cache/target directory.
    - To revert a modified tracked file when `git checkout -- <path>` fails
      because it cannot acquire `index.lock`, restore it from the commit tree:
      `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`.
    - Read-only inspection commands such as `git status --short` succeed with
      `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

    A long build or test command's completion must be confirmed by a positive
    marker in its captured output (`test result:`, `Finished`, or the target's
    own final line), with its absence treated as "did not run" regardless of the
    reported exit status.

    for open work covering the same problem. File each confirmed finding with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["qa-sweep"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Give it severity-appropriate priority and put the relevant commits, observed
    evidence, and exact reproduction steps in its description. Derive canonical
    `file:` selectors from every evidenced source path, removing the line suffix,
    and add the matching regression-test location. Use existing paths where
    possible; for a test file that must be created, set
    `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that intended path. Never file a
    finding without context selectors. Skip duplicates. Add `ui` to the tags
    of a finding in something a user sees (dashboard, web pages, docs site,
    desktop app UI), and attach its screenshot to the filed task with
    `orbit.task.artifact.put` at a stable path such as
    `screenshots/<view>-<theme>-<width>.png`, under the 1 MiB artifact limit:
    `.orbit/tmp/` is cleared with the worktree.

    subjects carry its ID as `[<task-id>]`; confirm with `orbit.task.show`), add
    `{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>","regression":{"nature":"<nature>","escape":"<escape>"}}`

    in the description instead. Never blame a bystander task.

    the link records:
    - `broke_existing`: the culprit broke behavior that worked before it landed.
    - `defect_in_new`: the defect is in code the culprit itself introduced.
    - `incomplete`: the culprit shipped without part of what its task required.
    - `merge_reintroduced`: a merge restored code or assets an earlier change had removed.
    - `contract_drift`: docs, schemas or a contract drifted from the behavior the culprit shipped.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the nature.

    - `no_test`: no test covered the broken behavior.
    - `test_not_selected`: a covering test existed but the delivery's gates did not run it.
    - `platform_only`: it shows only on a platform or host the gates did not exercise.
    - `review_missed`: it was visible in the diff and review did not flag it.
    - `spec_ambiguous`: the task or spec left the expected behavior open to the shipped reading.
    - `nondeterministic`: it depends on timing, ordering or environment and passed when gated.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the escape.

    A non-duplicate failing test that blocks the repository's
    standard validation command must be filed as a durable issue even when
    the failure is sandbox-specific, platform-specific, or otherwise
    environment-specific, including test-harness or portability defects.
    Do not leave such a breaking test in narrative-only output. Distinguish
    clearly between validation impact (the prescribed suite cannot complete)
    and production impact (whether the failure demonstrates a production
    defect). Include the failing command, the exact error, relevant
    environment evidence, and a scope assessment.

    Record the candidate revision you validated as this task's machine-readable
    cursor artifact, `sweep-cursor.json`, which the scheduler reads to decide
    whether the next tick has anything left to validate. Its exact content is
    `{"schema_version":1,"ref":"<integration branch>","cursor":"<full 40-character commit SHA>"}`;
    write it to `.orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json` and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json","path":"sweep-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    `orbit tool show <tool.name>` prints the tool's schema. Write it on every
    completed sweep, including one that found nothing to fix — a sweep without
    it leaves the next tick no cursor to compare the branch tip against.

    Your narrative output is advisory; the issues you file are the durable
    side-effect channel.

    ## Persist the execution summary

    In an ordinary managed activity, persist a meaningful `execution_summary`
    on this task with `orbit.task.update` before finishing. Include the
    validated revision, each command run with a passed, failed, or not-run
    outcome, any coverage gaps, and the filed task IDs; when no issues were
    found, state "no repository changes". A successful agent response does not
    substitute for persisting this task field.

    In claimed mode, `orbit.task.update` is unavailable. Return the same
    execution summary in the output so the owner can import it.

  - Real, non-duplicate issues were filed on the workspace's configured task or issue surface with evidence and reproduction steps.
  - The validated candidate revision is attached as this task's `sweep-cursor.json` artifact (`schema_version` 1, the integration branch, and the full commit SHA).

  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  status: backlog

run-failure-patterns.1c86c8f315b4b3db27e1ecf288d824d521fe44bf:
schemaVersion: 1
name: run-failure-patterns
description: Weekly mining of this workspace's run evidence for recurring failures that nobody has filed
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 20 7 * * 1
template:
  title: Mine recurring run failures
  description: |-
    Mine this workspace's own run evidence for recurring failure patterns that
    are not yet tracked. The durable output is one friction record or proposed
    task per untracked pattern plus the recorded scan cursor; the execution
    summary is the audit trail. Narrative-only output does not count as delivery.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Read-only against run state. Never retry, resume, cancel, or edit a run,
      and never change the status of a task a run touched. Read runs only with
      `orbit run history --limit <n> --json`, `orbit run show <run-id> --json`,
      `orbit run logs <run-id>`, and `orbit run events <run-id>`; do not read or
      edit the Orbit database or state files directly.
    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface for records. Find the newest completed
      prior instance with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["run-failure-patterns","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      (tag filters use AND semantics) and read its cursor artifact with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"run-failure-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Search existing coverage with
      `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<one distinctive token>","kind":"all","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and inspect a candidate with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Lexical search matches one case-insensitive substring: pass a single
      distinctive token (an error code, step name, or tool name), never a
      multi-word phrase, and do not treat a 0-hit multi-word query as proof that
      nothing covers the pattern.
    - File a pattern with
      `orbit tool run orbit.friction.add --input '{"title":"<surface and failure>","body":"<markdown>","tags":["automation"],"during_task":"<this task ID>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
      or, only when the fix is clear, propose a task (tool-created tasks start
      `proposed`) with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["run-failure-patterns"],"type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Fail open. A window with no new untracked pattern is a successful no-op. Do
      not invent work to justify the run.

    ## Determine the scan window

    Run the prior-instance query above. When it returns a task, read its
    `run-failure-cursor.json` artifact; its `cursor` is the RFC 3339 upper bound
    that instance scanned through, and this scan starts strictly after it. A
    selected instance without a readable cursor artifact is an error to report,
    not a first run: fall back to the cursor recorded in its execution summary,
    and fail the task if neither exists. Only when no prior instance exists, start
    the window seven days before now. The window ends at the moment this scan
    starts; record that timestamp before reading any run.

    The window contains every run whose `finished_at` falls inside it. Page
    `orbit run history --limit <n> --json` (newest first by creation) by raising
    `<n>` until the oldest returned run was created at least seven days before
    the window start, so long-running runs that finished inside the window are
    included. Runs still `pending` or `running` at scan start belong to the
    window in which they finish.

    ## Collect failure evidence

    From the window, collect:

    1. Runs whose state is `failed` or `interrupted`, and `cancelled` runs that
       recorded an error message.
    2. Step failure records: every non-success, non-skipped entry in a run's
       `steps` list, including failed steps inside runs that later succeeded
       after a retry or a recovery activity such as `step_failure_recovery`.
       Use `orbit run show <run-id> --json` for the step detail.
    3. Worker log evidence for those runs from `orbit run logs <run-id>` (and
       `--step <step-id>` for one step), read only as far as needed to name the
       error.

    ## Cluster by normalized signature

    Normalize each failure to a signature of error class, failing step, and
    tool: the error class is the stable code or leading error kind (for example
    an `error.code=` value, an HTTP status, or the failing guard name); the
    failing step is the step or deterministic action named in the error; the
    tool is the provider CLI, Orbit tool, or command that raised it. Strip run
    ids, task ids, timestamps, paths, SHAs, and counts before comparing, and
    group by the signature with the job ID as context.

    A cluster is a pattern only when it has **at least 3 occurrences across at
    least 2 distinct runs** in the window. One-offs and single-run retry loops
    below that threshold are not filed; count them in the summary only.

    ## Check coverage before filing

    For each pattern, search open and closed tasks and frictions with one
    distinctive token at a time from its signature (the error code, the step
    name, the tool name), and inspect every plausible hit. A pattern is already
    tracked when an open task or open friction describes the same underlying
    failure, or a done task does and no occurrence postdates its completion;
    record the `<signature> -> <id>` mapping and do not file. Occurrences after
    a done fix are a regression: file them as a new pattern that names the done
    task. Never file duplicates, including two records for one pattern in the
    same scan.

    ## File untracked patterns

    File exactly one record per untracked pattern: a friction by default, or a
    proposed task when the evidence makes the fix clear. The body states the
    normalized signature, occurrence count, distinct run count, first and last
    seen timestamps, up to three representative run ids, the affected job IDs,
    and one short excerpt of the error.

    Excerpts must be redacted. Quote at most a few lines, and replace tokens,
    credentials, authorization headers, cookies, email addresses, and home or
    user paths with placeholders before writing. Put excerpts only in text sent
    through `orbit.friction.add` or `orbit.task.add`, which also apply Orbit's
    write-time redaction; when the response reports `redactions_applied: true`,
    read the record back and confirm no secret-bearing context survived. Never
    attach raw logs as artifacts or copy them into other files.

    ## Record the cursor

    Always record the window bounds and the new cursor (the scan start
    timestamp) in the persisted execution summary, with runs scanned, failures
    collected, patterns found, filed ids, and already-tracked mappings. Write
    `{"schema_version":1,"cursor":"<RFC 3339 scan start>","runs_scanned":<count>}`
    to `.orbit/tmp/run-failure-cursor.json` (`$ORBIT_SCRATCH_DIR`) and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/run-failure-cursor.json","path":"run-failure-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Write it on every completed scan, including an empty window.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - The scan window started at the previous completed instance's recorded cursor, or seven days before the scan on the first run, and ended at the recorded scan start.
  - Failures were clustered by normalized signature, and only clusters with at least 3 occurrences across at least 2 distinct runs were treated as patterns.
  - Open and closed tasks and frictions were searched for every pattern before filing, and no duplicate record was filed.
  - Every filed record carries the signature, occurrence count, first and last seen, representative run ids, and a redacted excerpt.
  - No run was retried, resumed, cancelled, or edited, and no run state was mutated.

       host's run history never lists it; its owner keeps the failure or
       release settlement the leaf sent. Each entry of
       `orbit run settlements --since <window start> --no-reconcile --json`

       `forge_unavailable`, `final_recovery`, `failure`, `summary`),

       are designed outcomes, not failures. A leaf run that also appears in
       this host's run history is one occurrence, not two. When the read

       replica checkout the list is empty; leave its claimed leaves (jobs

       owner's scan, which counts them from these settlements.

    `pipeline_success_guard`. Fold parents by the recorded cause, never by
    judgment or by matching error text: read `root_cause` from

    tool: the error class is the stable code or leading error kind (for example
    an `error.code=` value, an HTTP status, the failing guard name, or a
    settlement's `evidence` and `failure_class`); the failing step is the step
    or deterministic action named in the error; the tool is the provider CLI,
    Orbit tool, or command that raised it. Strip run ids, task ids, timestamps,
    paths, SHAs, host names, and counts before comparing, and group by the

    host and on a follower is one pattern.

      asking for evidence the reviewer's host cannot produce: a native OS

      revisions, such as `validation_incomplete` for a required check an
      earlier revision recorded and the final one omits, a superseded attempt
      with no replacing pass, or a report or certificate mismatch.

      acceptance criteria or approach must change.
    - `timeout`: the reviewer exceeded its wall clock or review budget.

    least 2 distinct runs** in the window. Below that threshold, a single
    occurrence is still a pattern when all of these hold:

      timeout clamp, a size cap), not a provider (authentication, capacity,
      rate limit), capacity or network error (DNS, TLS, status 000, a
      connection reset), which stay counted only;
    - it blocked a task (the task is `blocked`, or its claim failed) or
      needed an operator rerun or resume;

      conditions.

    distinctive token at a time from its signature (the error code, the step
    name, the tool name, the escalation category), and inspect every plausible

    `proposed` one) or open friction describes the same underlying failure, a
    done task does and no occurrence postdates its completion, or a rejected
    task's rationale decided the same failure is not to be fixed; record the
    `<signature> -> <id>` mapping and do not file. Occurrences after a done fix
    are a regression: file them as a new pattern that names the done task.
    Never file duplicates, including two records for one pattern in the same
    scan.

    For every untracked pattern, find the mechanism in this checkout, which
    is at the workspace's current integration base; record
    `git rev-parse HEAD`. Name the file and function that raise or permit the
    failure, and quote the guard, comment or constant that explains it (a
    few lines). A pattern whose cause the evidence and code cannot establish
    is filed as a friction, not a task.

    ## File untracked patterns

    File exactly one record per untracked pattern: a proposed fix task, or a
    friction when no cause could be established. The body carries:

    - the problem, in a sentence or two;
    - an evidence table: normalized signature, occurrence count, distinct
      run count, hosts, first and last seen timestamps, up to three
      representative run ids, the affected job IDs, and one short redacted
      excerpt;
    - the verified mechanism: file, function, quoted guard and commit;

      `context_files` naming the verified files, and an assessed complexity.

    pattern, including one that reintroduced a done fix, add

    the link records:
    - `broke_existing`: the culprit broke behavior that worked before it landed.
    - `defect_in_new`: the defect is in code the culprit itself introduced.
    - `incomplete`: the culprit shipped without part of what its task required.
    - `merge_reintroduced`: a merge restored code or assets an earlier change had removed.
    - `contract_drift`: docs, schemas or a contract drifted from the behavior the culprit shipped.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the nature.
    `escape` is why the delivery gates missed it:
    - `no_test`: no test covered the broken behavior.
    - `test_not_selected`: a covering test existed but the delivery's gates did not run it.
    - `platform_only`: it shows only on a platform or host the gates did not exercise.
    - `review_missed`: it was visible in the diff and review did not flag it.
    - `spec_ambiguous`: the task or spec left the expected behavior open to the shipped reading.
    - `nondeterministic`: it depends on timing, ordering or environment and passed when gated.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the escape.

    Excerpts must be redacted. Quote at most a few lines, and replace tokens,
    credentials, authorization headers, cookies, email addresses, and home or

    to `.orbit/tmp/run-failure-cursor.json` (`$ORBIT_SCRATCH_DIR`) and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/run-failure-cursor.json","path":"run-failure-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    `orbit tool show <tool.name>` prints the tool's schema.

    the recorded scan cursor; the execution summary is the audit trail.

      coordination commit.

      and inspect a candidate with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Lexical search matches one case-insensitive substring: pass a single
      distinctive token (an error code, step name, or tool name), never a
      multi-word phrase, and do not treat a 0-hit multi-word query as proof that
      nothing covers the pattern.

      task-authoring reference (`references/task-authoring.md`) and follow it
      for task shape. File each fix task (tool-created tasks start `proposed`)
      with

      an `--approve-proposed` drain never promotes it. File a friction instead
      only when the evidence cannot establish a cause, with
      `orbit tool run orbit.friction.add --input '{"title":"<surface and failure>","body":"<markdown>","tags":["automation"],"during_task":"<this task ID>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.

      tasks, so a friction beside a fix task duplicates the work. Do not use
      direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.

      not invent work to justify the run.

    Run the prior-instance query above. When it returns a task, read its
    `run-failure-cursor.json` artifact; its `cursor` is the RFC 3339 upper bound
    that instance scanned through, and this scan starts strictly after it. A
    selected instance without a readable cursor artifact is an error to report,
    not a first run: fall back to the cursor recorded in its execution summary,
    and fail the task if neither exists. Only when no prior instance exists, start
    the window seven days before now. The window ends at the moment this scan
    starts; record that timestamp before reading any run.

    The window contains every run whose `finished_at` falls inside it. Page
    `orbit run history --limit <n> --no-reconcile --json` (newest first by
    creation) by raising `<n>` until the oldest returned run was created at
    least seven days before the window start, so long-running runs that
    finished inside the window are included. Runs still `pending` or `running` at scan start belong to the
    window in which they finish.

    From the window, collect:

    1. Runs whose state is `failed` or `interrupted`, and `cancelled` runs that
       recorded an error message.
    2. Step failure records: every non-success, non-skipped entry in a run's
       `steps` list, including failed steps inside runs that later succeeded
       after a retry or a recovery activity such as `step_failure_recovery`.

       `orbit run logs <run-id> --no-reconcile` (and `--step <step-id>` for one
       step), read only as far as needed to name the error.

       host's run history never lists it; its owner keeps the failure or
       release settlement the leaf sent. Each entry of
       `orbit run settlements --since <window start> --no-reconcile --json`
       whose `settled_at` falls in the window is one occurrence in one run

       `evidence` names the class (`provider_unavailable`, `baseline_red`,
       `forge_unavailable`, `final_recovery`, `failure`, `summary`),
       `failure_class` the typed failure, `failed_step_id` the step, and
       `reason` the leaf's own diagnostic. An `unrecorded` entry settled
       before the owner kept settlements: take its reason from the task's
       history `note` or comment at `settled_at` through `orbit.task.show`.

       are designed outcomes, not failures. A leaf run that also appears in
       this host's run history is one occurrence, not two. When the read
       refuses because a coordination commit is pending, record that in the
       summary and continue without follower evidence. In a follower's
       replica checkout the list is empty; leave its claimed leaves (jobs
       `task_claimed_pr_pipeline` and `task_claimed_local_pipeline`) to the
       owner's scan, which counts them from these settlements.

    ## Fold cascades by recorded cause

    A parent pipeline whose child fails also fails, in
    `pipeline_success_guard`. Fold parents by the recorded cause, never by
    judgment or by matching error text: read `root_cause` from
    `orbit run show <run-id> --no-reconcile --json` for every failed run.
    When `root_cause.run_id` names another run, the run is an echo of that
    run: count the occurrence once, at the root cause. When the root cause is
    a `pipeline_success_guard` failure, read its run's
    `pipeline_state.child_dispatches[].child_run_id` and their states: a
    `held` child is a designed hold (review evidence, a red base, a forge
    outage), so neither that run nor any parent folded into it is a failure.
    Report the fold count and the held-chain count in the summary.

    ## Cluster by normalized signature

    Normalize each failure to a signature of error class, failing step, and
    tool: the error class is the stable code or leading error kind (for example
    an `error.code=` value, an HTTP status, the failing guard name, or a
    settlement's `evidence` and `failure_class`); the failing step is the step
    or deterministic action named in the error; the tool is the provider CLI,
    Orbit tool, or command that raised it. Strip run ids, task ids, timestamps,
    paths, SHAs, host names, and counts before comparing, and group by the
    signature with the job ID and host as context. One pattern seen on this
    host and on a follower is one pattern.

    Split review refusals. A `review_gate_settle` or `review` refusal also
    carries an escalation category, read from the refusal's error message
    (`review_gate_blocked: verdict <verdict> (<escalation>)`, a
    `[baseline_red]` marker, or `review_timeout_incomplete`; a follower
    settlement's `reason`) and, for the
    task's latest attempt, from the stored review evidence read with
    `orbit.task.artifact.get`: `review-gate.json` (`verdict`, `escalation`)
    and `review-report.json` (`verdict`, `escalation`, `external_evidence`,
    and each `validation[]` record's `outcome` and `role`). Each category is a
    pattern by itself:

    - `base_red`: a `[baseline_red]` refusal, or an escalation saying a
      required check fails on the base, is pre-existing, or needs a green base.
    - `external_evidence`: a non-empty `external_evidence`, or an escalation
      asking for evidence the reviewer's host cannot produce: a native OS
      (`native_os`), a hosted CI result (`hosted_ci`), or CodeQL (`codeql`).
    - `report_revision`: the gate refused the reviewer's report or its
      revisions, such as `validation_incomplete` for a required check an
      earlier revision recorded and the final one omits, a superseded attempt
      with no replacing pass, or a report or certificate mismatch.
    - `scope_or_criteria`: a `reject` whose escalation says the task's scope,
      acceptance criteria or approach must change.
    - `timeout`: the reviewer exceeded its wall clock or review budget.
    - `other`: anything else.

    A cluster is a pattern when it has **at least 3 occurrences across at
    least 2 distinct runs** in the window. Below that threshold, a single
    occurrence is still a pattern when all of these hold:

    - it came from a deterministic Orbit action (a step such as `git_push`,
      `git_commit`, `pr_open`, `pr_complete` or a guard) or a tool limit (a
      timeout clamp, a size cap), not a provider (authentication, capacity,
      rate limit), capacity or network error (DNS, TLS, status 000, a
      connection reset), which stay counted only;
    - it blocked a task (the task is `blocked`, or its claim failed) or
      needed an operator rerun or resume;
    - the code verification below shows it would recur under the same
      conditions.

    Count every other one-off and single-run retry loop in the summary only.

    ## Check coverage before filing

    For each pattern, search open and closed tasks and frictions with one
    distinctive token at a time from its signature (the error code, the step
    name, the tool name, the escalation category), and inspect every plausible
    hit. A pattern is already tracked when an open task (including a
    `proposed` one) or open friction describes the same underlying failure, a
    done task does and no occurrence postdates its completion, or a rejected
    task's rationale decided the same failure is not to be fixed; record the
    `<signature> -> <id>` mapping and do not file. Occurrences after a done fix
    are a regression: file them as a new pattern that names the done task.
    Never file duplicates, including two records for one pattern in the same
    scan.

    ## Verify the mechanism in code

    For every untracked pattern, find the mechanism in this checkout, which
    is at the workspace's current integration base; record
    `git rev-parse HEAD`. Name the file and function that raise or permit the
    failure, and quote the guard, comment or constant that explains it (a
    few lines). A pattern whose cause the evidence and code cannot establish
    is filed as a friction, not a task.

    ## File untracked patterns

    File exactly one record per untracked pattern: a proposed fix task, or a
    friction when no cause could be established. The body carries:

    - the problem, in a sentence or two;
    - an evidence table: normalized signature, occurrence count, distinct
      run count, hosts, first and last seen timestamps, up to three
      representative run ids, the affected job IDs, and one short redacted
      excerpt;
    - the verified mechanism: file, function, quoted guard and commit;
    - for a task, the proposed change; then observable acceptance criteria,
      `context_files` naming the verified files, and an assessed complexity.

    When the verified mechanism shows that a landed task's change caused the
    pattern, including one that reintroduced a done fix, add
    `{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>","regression":{"nature":"<nature>","escape":"<escape>"}}`
    to the fix task's `relations` and name that commit in its body. Never blame
    a bystander task.
    Choose `unclassified` rather than guess. `nature` is what kind of regression
    the link records:
    - `broke_existing`: the culprit broke behavior that worked before it landed.
    - `defect_in_new`: the defect is in code the culprit itself introduced.
    - `incomplete`: the culprit shipped without part of what its task required.
    - `merge_reintroduced`: a merge restored code or assets an earlier change had removed.
    - `contract_drift`: docs, schemas or a contract drifted from the behavior the culprit shipped.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the nature.
    `escape` is why the delivery gates missed it:
    - `no_test`: no test covered the broken behavior.
    - `test_not_selected`: a covering test existed but the delivery's gates did not run it.
    - `platform_only`: it shows only on a platform or host the gates did not exercise.
    - `review_missed`: it was visible in the diff and review did not flag it.
    - `spec_ambiguous`: the task or spec left the expected behavior open to the shipped reading.
    - `nondeterministic`: it depends on timing, ordering or environment and passed when gated.
    - `unclassified`: the evidence does not settle the escape.

    Excerpts must be redacted. Quote at most a few lines, and replace tokens,
    credentials, authorization headers, cookies, email addresses, and home or
    user paths with placeholders before writing. Put excerpts only in text sent
    through `orbit.friction.add` or `orbit.task.add`, which also apply Orbit's
    write-time redaction; when the response reports `redactions_applied: true`,
    read the record back and confirm no secret-bearing context survived. Never
    attach raw logs as artifacts or copy them into other files.

    ## Record the cursor

    Always record the window bounds and the new cursor (the scan start
    timestamp) in the persisted execution summary, with runs scanned,
    follower settlements read, failures collected, the fold and held-chain
    counts, patterns found, filed ids, already-tracked mappings, and the
    one-offs counted but not filed. Write
    `{"schema_version":1,"cursor":"<RFC 3339 scan start>","runs_scanned":<count>}`
    to `.orbit/tmp/run-failure-cursor.json` (`$ORBIT_SCRATCH_DIR`) and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/run-failure-cursor.json","path":"run-failure-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    `orbit tool show <tool.name>` prints the tool's schema.
    Write it on every completed scan, including an empty window.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - The scan window started at the previous completed instance's recorded cursor, or seven days before the scan on the first run, and ended at the recorded scan start.
  - Follower leaf settlements from `orbit run settlements --no-reconcile` were counted with this host's runs, and failed parents were folded by their recorded `root_cause`, with a held child's parents not counted as failures.
  - Failures were clustered by normalized signature, with review refusals split by escalation category, and only clusters with at least 3 occurrences across at least 2 distinct runs, or a blocking deterministic Orbit-action or tool-limit one-off, were treated as patterns.
  - Open and closed tasks and frictions were searched for every pattern before filing, and no duplicate record was filed.
  - Every untracked pattern's mechanism was verified in code, and it was filed as one proposed fix task tagged `run-failure-patterns` and `no-auto-approve`, or as a friction only when no cause could be established, never both.
  - Every filed record carries the signature, occurrence count, first and last seen, representative run ids, and a redacted excerpt.
  - No run was retried, resumed, cancelled, or edited, and no run state was mutated.
  - The execution summary reports runs scanned, patterns found, filed versus already-tracked ids, and the window bounds, and the new cursor is attached as `run-failure-cursor.json`.
  - A window with no new untracked pattern succeeds as a no-op.

  - run-failure-patterns

  - orbit.search
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.artifact.get
  - orbit.task.artifact.put
  - orbit.task.list
  - orbit.task.show

name: run-failure-patterns
description: Weekly mining of this workspace's run evidence for recurring failures that nobody has filed
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 20 7 * * 1
template:
  title: Mine recurring run failures
  description: |-
    Mine this workspace's own run evidence for recurring failure patterns that
    are not yet tracked. The durable output is one proposed fix task per
    untracked pattern (a friction only when no cause can be established) plus
    the recorded scan cursor; the execution summary is the audit trail.
    Narrative-only output does not count as delivery.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Read-only against run state. Never retry, resume, cancel, or edit a run,
      and never change the status of a task a run touched. Read runs only with
      `orbit run history --limit <n> --no-reconcile --json`,
      `orbit run show <run-id> --no-reconcile --json`,
      `orbit run logs <run-id> --no-reconcile`, and
      `orbit run events <run-id> --no-reconcile`, and read the settlements
      claimed leaves on follower hosts sent this owner only with
      `orbit run settlements --since <window start> --no-reconcile --json`;
      do not read or edit the Orbit database or state files directly. Never
      drop `--no-reconcile`: without it the run reads finalize an orphaned
      `pending` or `running` run as `interrupted` and release its task
      reservations, and the settlement read recovers an interrupted
      coordination commit.
    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface for records. Find the newest completed
      prior instance with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["run-failure-patterns","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      (tag filters use AND semantics) and read its cursor artifact with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"run-failure-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Search existing coverage with
      `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<one distinctive token>","kind":"all","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and inspect a candidate with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Lexical search matches one case-insensitive substring: pass a single
      distinctive token (an error code, step name, or tool name), never a
      multi-word phrase, and do not treat a 0-hit multi-word query as proof that
      nothing covers the pattern.
    - Before filing a fix task, read the installed `orbit` skill's
      task-authoring reference (`references/task-authoring.md`) and follow it
      for task shape. File each fix task (tool-created tasks start `proposed`)
      with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<surface and failure>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"context_files":["file:<verified path>"],"complexity":"<assessed>","tags":["run-failure-patterns","no-auto-approve"],"type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Add `"crew":"opus"` when the assessed complexity is `hard` or `xhard`.
      The `no-auto-approve` tag keeps the task `proposed` for human approval:
      an `--approve-proposed` drain never promotes it. File a friction instead
      only when the evidence cannot establish a cause, with
      `orbit tool run orbit.friction.add --input '{"title":"<surface and failure>","body":"<markdown>","tags":["automation","run-failure-patterns"],"during_task":"<this task ID>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.

      tasks, so a friction beside a fix task duplicates the work. Do not use
      direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Fail open. A window with no new untracked pattern is a successful no-op. Do
      not invent work to justify the run.

    ## Determine the scan window

    Run the prior-instance query above. When it returns a task, read its
    `run-failure-cursor.json` artifact; its `cursor` is the RFC 3339 upper bound
    that instance scanned through, and this scan starts strictly after it. A
    selected instance without a readable cursor artifact is an error to report,
    not a first run: fall back to the cursor recorded in its execution summary,
    and fail the task if neither exists. Only when no prior instance exists, start
    the window seven days before now. The window ends at the moment this scan
    starts; record that timestamp before reading any run.

    The window contains every run whose `finished_at` falls inside it. Page
    `orbit run history --limit <n> --no-reconcile --json` (newest first by
    creation) by raising `<n>` until the oldest returned run was created at
    least seven days before the window start, so long-running runs that
    finished inside the window are included. Runs still `pending` or `running` at scan start belong to the
    window in which they finish.

    From the window, collect:

    1. Runs whose state is `failed` or `interrupted`, and `cancelled` runs that
       recorded an error message.
    2. Step failure records: every non-success, non-skipped entry in a run's
       `steps` list, including failed steps inside runs that later succeeded
       after a retry or a recovery activity such as `step_failure_recovery`.

    3. Worker log evidence for those runs from
       `orbit run logs <run-id> --no-reconcile` (and `--step <step-id>` for one
       step), read only as far as needed to name the error.
    4. Follower leaf failures. A claimed leaf runs on a follower host, so this
       host's run history never lists it; its owner keeps the failure or
       release settlement the leaf sent. Each entry of
       `orbit run settlements --since <window start> --no-reconcile --json`
       whose `settled_at` falls in the window is one occurrence in one run
       (its `leaf_run_id`) on host `machine_name` or `machine_id`. Its
       `evidence` names the class (`provider_unavailable`, `baseline_red`,
       `forge_unavailable`, `final_recovery`, `failure`, `summary`),
       `failure_class` the typed failure, `failed_step_id` the step, and
       `reason` the leaf's own diagnostic. An `unrecorded` entry settled
       before the owner kept settlements: take its reason from the task's
       history `note` or comment at `settled_at` through `orbit.task.show`.

       are designed outcomes, not failures. A leaf run that also appears in
       this host's run history is one occurrence, not two. When the read
       refuses because a coordination commit is pending, record that in the
       summary and continue without follower evidence. In a follower's
       replica checkout the list is empty; leave its claimed leaves (jobs
       `task_claimed_pr_pipeline` and `task_claimed_local_pipeline`) to the
       owner's scan, which counts them from these settlements.
